definition_zh: 耕种；栽培；（微生物的）培养；修养；培养（能力、关系）
definition_en: the act of tilling land, growing crops or organisms, or developing a quality, person or relationship through sustained care
core_image: 一块被反复翻土、除草、浇水的田，土面松软，作物按行生长，田边放着种子袋与记录本
scene: 田垄被翻得松软，农人蹲下检查幼苗的根系，远处水渠正缓缓放水。Careful cultivation keeps the seed bed open to air and water.
sceneCN: 这里指「对土地反复翻耕与照管」（第 1 个义项：耕作土地）；句意为细致的耕作让苗床保持通气与水分。

pos.zh: 耕种；栽培；（微生物）培养；修养（多作不可数名词）

forms.label: 相关名词（耕作的人或机具）

derivatives.zh: cultivate + -able（能……的）→ 可耕种的；可培养的
cultivate + -or（施动者或工具）→ 耕作的人；中耕机
cultivate + -ar（名词后缀，二十世纪园艺用语）→ 栽培品种（语义偏移：从动作转为被栽培的品系）
cultivate + -ed（过去分词作形容词）→ 耕作的；有教养的
un-（否定）+ cultivated → 未开垦的；未受教育的
re-（重新）+ cultivate → 重新耕作（语义偏移：荒废之后再翻种）

senses.title: Break and tend the soil
senses.definition: to prepare land by ploughing, digging and weeding so that crops can grow
senses.definitionCN: 通过犁翻、挖掘与除草备好土地，使作物得以生长
senses.example: Cultivation of the heavy clay begins in early spring.
senses.exampleCN: 对这种重黏土的耕作从早春开始。
senses.why: The Latin root colere meant to till and to dwell on land, so the first sense is simply the farmer's work on the soil.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 colere 本义是耕作、居住于土地，因此第一义就是农人对土壤的劳作。

senses.title: Growing a named crop
senses.definition: the raising of a particular crop on prepared land, as in rice cultivation
senses.definitionCN: 在备好的土地上种植特定作物，如水稻种植
senses.example: Rice cultivation requires level fields and steady water.
senses.exampleCN: 水稻种植需要平整的田块与稳定的水。
senses.why: Once land is prepared, the same word names the crop put into it, because the whole cycle counts as one practice.
senses.whyCN: 土地备好之后，同一个词就指种进去的作物，因为整个周期算作一项实践。

senses.title: Raising garden plants or trees
senses.definition: the deliberate growing of ornamental plants, fruit trees or forest seedlings
senses.definitionCN: 有意栽培观赏植物、果树或林木幼苗
senses.example: The cultivation of olives spread along the coast.
senses.exampleCN: 橄榄的栽培沿海岸传播开来。
senses.why: The verb extended from field crops to any plant that people tend rather than gather wild.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词从田里的作物扩展到任何由人照管、而非野外采集的植物。

senses.title: Growing microorganisms in a medium
senses.titleCN: 在培养基中培养微生物
senses.definition: the controlled growth of bacteria, cells or tissue in a prepared medium
senses.definitionCN: 在配好的培养基中受控地培养细菌、细胞或组织
senses.example: Cultivation of the sample revealed two distinct bacterial colonies.
senses.exampleCN: 对样本的培养显示出两种不同的菌落。
senses.why: Nineteenth-century microbiology borrowed the agricultural word because a culture dish is a small field where organisms are fed and grown.
senses.whyCN: 十九世纪的微生物学借用了农业词，因为培养皿就是一块喂养、培育生物的小田。

senses.title: Developing a skill or habit
senses.definition: the gradual development of an ability, habit or quality through repeated practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复练习逐步发展某种能力、习惯或品质
senses.example: Cultivation of patience takes longer than learning the rules.
senses.exampleCN: 培养耐心比学会规则要花更长时间。
senses.why: Growing a plant and growing a habit share one shape: small repeated acts of care produce a result that cannot be rushed.
senses.whyCN: 种植植物与培养习惯形状相同：反复的小小照料产生无法催快的结果。

senses.title: Keeping a relationship or contact
senses.definition: the deliberate effort to maintain a friendship, contact or useful connection
senses.definitionCN: 有意维持友谊、联系或有用的关系
senses.example: The diplomat's cultivation of local leaders lasted years.
senses.exampleCN: 这位外交官对当地领袖的经营持续多年。
senses.why: A relationship, like a crop, needs regular attention; neglect is the weed that takes it over.
senses.whyCN: 关系如同作物，需要定期照料；疏忽就是接管它的杂草。

senses.title: Refinement of mind and manners
senses.definition: the refined state of a person's mind, taste or manners, produced by education and good company
senses.definitionCN: 由教育与良好交往造就的心智、趣味或举止上的修养
senses.example: Her cultivation showed in the way she listened before answering.
senses.exampleCN: 她的修养体现在先听完再回答的方式上。
senses.why: The metaphor turns inward: what is tilled is no longer soil but the person, and the harvest is poise rather than grain.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻转向内部：被耕的不再是土壤而是人，收获的也不是谷物而是从容。

senses.title: Guiding a person's growth
senses.definition: the work of developing someone's abilities and character under sustained guidance
senses.definitionCN: 在持续指导下发展某人的能力与品格
senses.example: The older musician's cultivation of young players saved the ensemble.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年长音乐家对年轻乐手的培养拯救了整个乐团。
senses.why: The agricultural image completes itself: a gardener who tends seedlings is a mentor who tends beginners.
senses.whyCN: 农业意象在此闭合：照看幼苗的园丁，就是照看初学者的师长。

intro.en: Cultivation comes from Latin cultura, a tilling or care, built on cultus, the past participle of colere, to till, inhabit or worship. The noun reached English through Middle French. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultivation 来自拉丁 cultura「耕作、照料」，其基础是 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」的过去分词 cultus。这个名词经中古法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Colere meant to till the soil, to dwell on land and to honour a god; Roman usage treated these as one act of tending. Its deeper root is generally connected with a verb meaning to turn or move around, but that link is a reconstruction.
items.cn: colere 意为耕作土地、居住于土地、敬奉神明；罗马用法把这三者视为同一种照料。它更深的词根一般认为与表示「转动、绕行」的动词有关，但这一联系属重构形式。

items.en: The past participle cultus described land that had been worked and a life that had been ordered; it also named care and worship.
items.cn: 过去分词 cultus 描述被耕作过的土地与被整理过的人生，也指照料与敬奉。

items.en: Cultura named the act of tilling and the care given to a field, a body or a mind; it is the direct source of the English noun.
items.cn: cultura 指耕作的行为，以及对田地、身体或心智的照料；它是这个英语名词的直接来源。

items.en: Middle French cultivation carried the learned noun into English in the fifteenth century, first in agricultural and religious writing.
items.cn: 中古法语 cultivation 在十五世纪把这个学术名词带入英语，最初用于农业与宗教文本。

items.en: From the late nineteenth century the word was used for growing microorganisms in a prepared medium, a sense borrowed from the image of a small cultivated field.
items.cn: 从十九世纪后期起，这个词用于在配好的培养基中培养微生物，这一义借自「一小块被耕作的田」的意象。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-Latin origin of colere is reconstructed rather than attested, and the earliest English use is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：colere 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构形式，并非有据可查；英语最早用例的年代也只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin root that name neighbouring things; group two holds verbs and nouns for the work of raising plants.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词根、指相邻事物的词；第二组是表示「培育植物」这项工作本身的动词与名词。

entries.definition: From the same Latin cultura but naming the whole way of life, arts and beliefs of a group, not the act of tilling.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁 cultura，却指一个群体的生活方式、艺术与信念整体，而非耕作行为。

entries.definition: From Latin cultus, it names a religious system or a devoted following, preserving the worship sense that agriculture dropped.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cultus，指宗教体系或狂热的追随群体，保留了农业义所丢弃的「敬奉」义。

entries.definition: Latin ager, field, plus cultura: the science and business of farming, broader than the care of one plot.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 ager「田地」加 cultura：农业的科学与产业，比单块土地的耕作更广。

entries.definition: Latin hortus, garden, plus cultura: the art of growing garden plants, narrower than cultivation in general.
entries.definitionCN: 拉丁 hortus「园子」加 cultura：栽培园艺植物的技艺，比泛指的 cultivation 更窄。

entries.definition: The mechanical working of soil, such as ploughing and harrowing; it stops at the soil and does not cover crops, microbes or manners.
entries.definitionCN: 对土壤的机械作业，如犁耕与耙地；只到土壤为止，不涵盖作物、微生物或举止。

entries.definition: The whole business of raising crops and animals; cultivation is one part of it, the care of soil and plants.
entries.definitionCN: 种植作物与饲养动物的整个产业；cultivation 只是其中一部分，即对土壤与植物的照料。

entries.definition: Care given to something while it grows, especially a child or a talent; it stresses the caring relationship rather than the technique.
entries.definitionCN: 对生长中之物的照料，尤指孩子或才能；强调照料关系而非技术。

entries.definition: The controlled reproduction of plants or animals to select desired traits; cultivation grows them, breeding chooses the stock.
entries.definitionCN: 为选育理想性状而控制植物或动物的繁殖；cultivation 负责栽培，breeding 负责选种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: colere 'to till' plus -ation 'the act': the act of tilling, and then of tending anything else.
normal.cn: colere「耕作」加 -ation「行为」：耕作的行为，随后扩展到照管别的东西。

normal.en: The family runs cultivate, cultivation, cultivator, cultivable, cultivar, cultivated.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cultivate、cultivation、cultivator、cultivable、cultivar、cultivated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: rice cultivation, shifting cultivation, intensive cultivation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出田间义：水稻种植、轮歇耕作、集约耕作。

normal.en: Laboratory use keeps the field image: a culture dish is a small plot for microbes.
normal.cn: 实验室用法保留田地意象：培养皿就是给微生物的一小块地。

normal.en: The inward sense appears in the fixed phrase cultivation of the mind.
normal.cn: 内向义出现在固定搭配「心性修养」中。

abstract.en: Picture a library where every shelf is a row of seedlings and the reader is the farmer.
abstract.cn: 想象一座图书馆，每一排书架都是一行幼苗，读者就是农夫。

abstract.en: Picture a friendship watered once a week, never flooded and never left dry.
abstract.cn: 想象一段每周浇一次水的关系，既不被淹没，也不被晒干。

abstract.en: Picture a violin teacher adjusting a beginner's hand as a gardener ties a young tree to a stake.
abstract.cn: 想象小提琴老师调整初学者的手，如同园丁把小树绑在支柱上。

examples.en: Terrace cultivation holds the soil on slopes that would otherwise wash away.
examples.cn: 梯田耕作保住了那些本来会被冲走的山坡土壤。

examples.en: The cultivation of bacteria requires sterile tools and a controlled temperature.
examples.cn: 培养细菌需要无菌器具与受控温度。

examples.en: His cultivation of the committee's trust made the reform possible.
examples.cn: 他对委员会信任的经营使改革成为可能。

dict_mnemonic.text: cult（耕种、培育）+ -ivation（行为）→ 反复照管让东西长起来；土地、细菌、才能、关系都能被培育，名词就是这一过程。

root: 拉丁 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」→ cultus「耕过的、受照料的」→ cultura「耕作、培育」→ 中世纪拉丁 cultivatio；colere 在拉丁语之前的词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: soil is broken, a crop is tended, and the same tending is then applied to microbes, skills, contacts, manners and a pupil.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：先翻土，再照管作物，随后把同一种照管用于微生物、技能、人脉、举止与学生。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field is broken, sown and weeded until the soil, the crop and finally the farmer's own mind are all under care.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块田被翻、被种、被除草，直到土壤、作物以及农夫自己的心智都处在照料之下。

branches.en: THE FIELD CYCLE: preparing ground and putting a named crop into it.
branches.cn: 田间周期：先备好地，再把某一种作物种进去。

branches.en: THE GARDEN: the same care applied to plants that are not field crops.
branches.cn: 园圃：把同一种照料用于并非田间作物的植物。

branches.en: THE DISH: a laboratory medium is a small field for invisible organisms.
branches.cn: 培养皿：培养基就是给看不见的生物的一小块田。

branches.en: REPEATED CARE: habits and friendships both grow by regular, unhurried attention.
branches.cn: 反复照料：习惯与友谊都靠规律而不急躁的关注生长。

branches.en: THE INWARD HARVEST: manners and pupils are the last crops, ripened by the same patience.
branches.cn: 内在的收获：举止与学生是最后的作物，由同一种耐心催熟。

intro.en: Cultivation is a Latin noun built from a verb root and a suffix, and both parts also build a large English family, so the word can be read morpheme by morpheme.
intro.cn: cultivation 是由动词词根与后缀构成的拉丁名词，这两部分还构成一个庞大的英语词族，因此可以按语素逐个读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin colere supplies cultus, cultura and cultivare; the suffix -ation turns a verb of tending into the name of the work or its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 colere 衍生出 cultus、cultura 与 cultivare；后缀 -ation 把表示照管的动词变成工作或其结果的名称。

items.meaning: to till; to dwell; to worship
items.example: The root names the whole act of tending land.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名照料土地的全部动作。

items.example: The participle became a noun for care and worship.
items.exampleCN: 这个分词转为表示照料与敬奉的名词。

items.example: Cultura is the direct ancestor of the English noun.
items.exampleCN: cultura 是这个英语名词的直接祖先。

items.example: Medieval Latin built a new verb from the old participle.
items.exampleCN: 中世纪拉丁语从旧分词造出一个新动词。

items.meaning: the work of tilling or tending
items.example: The noun names the work and its result.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指工作及其结果。

items.example: The suffix also builds preservation and navigation.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀还构成 preservation 与 navigation。

items.structure: cultivate + -or (one who acts or a tool)
items.meaning: a person or machine that tills
items.example: The cultivator loosened the rows between the vines.
items.exampleCN: 中耕机松开了藤行之间的土。

items.meaning: able to be tilled or grown
items.example: Only the valley floor is cultivable.
items.exampleCN: 只有谷底可以耕种。

items.example: The cultivated slope held its soil.
items.exampleCN: 这块被耕作的坡地保住了土壤。

items.example: The new cultivar resists mildew.
items.exampleCN: 这个新品种抗白粉病。

sceneCN: 这里指「翻耕土地并种植作物」（第 1 个义项：耕作土地）；句意为农民用牛拉的犁耕作低处的田地。

senses.title: Till the ground and grow a crop
senses.definition: to prepare land by ploughing or digging and then grow crops on it
senses.definitionCN: 通过犁翻或挖掘备好土地，然后在其上种植作物
senses.example: They cultivate the valley floor in narrow strips.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把谷底分成窄条来耕种。
senses.why: The verb is the action behind cultivation, so its first sense is the farmer's direct work on the ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词是 cultivation 背后的动作，因此第一义就是农人对土地的直接劳作。

senses.title: Raise garden plants
senses.definition: to grow and tend plants in a garden, orchard or nursery
senses.definitionCN: 在园圃、果园或苗圃中种植并照管植物
senses.example: She cultivates roses along the south wall.
senses.exampleCN: 她沿南墙栽培玫瑰。
senses.why: The same action moves from open fields to enclosed gardens, where tending matters more than area.
senses.whyCN: 同一动作从大田移到围起的园子，在那里照料比面积更重要。

senses.title: Grow bacteria or cells
senses.definition: to grow microorganisms or living cells in a prepared medium under controlled conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在配好的培养基中、受控条件下培养微生物或活细胞
senses.example: The lab cultivates the strain at body temperature.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在体温条件下培养这一菌株。
senses.why: A culture dish repeats the field: a contained surface, added nutrients and a population left to multiply.
senses.whyCN: 培养皿重复了田地的结构：一块围住的表面、加入的养分，以及任其繁殖的群体。

senses.title: Develop a skill or habit
senses.definition: to develop an ability, habit or quality by repeated practice
senses.definitionCN: 通过反复练习发展某种能力、习惯或品质
senses.example: He cultivates the habit of reading before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他养成了黎明前读书的习惯。
senses.why: A habit grows the way a plant does: slowly, from repeated small acts rather than one large effort.
senses.whyCN: 习惯的生长方式如同植物：缓慢，来自反复的小动作，而非一次大力气。

senses.title: Build a friendship
senses.definition: to give deliberate time and attention to a friendship or connection
senses.definitionCN: 有意为友谊或联系投入时间与关注
senses.example: They cultivate their friendship over long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们靠长途散步来经营友谊。
senses.why: Friendship is treated as a living thing that dies if it is never watered by contact.
senses.whyCN: 友谊被当作活物：若从不以联络浇水，它就会枯死。

senses.title: Mentor a person
senses.definition: to help someone's abilities and character develop through sustained guidance
senses.definitionCN: 通过持续指导帮助某人的能力与品格发展
senses.example: The coach cultivates young players rather than replacing them.
senses.exampleCN: 教练培养年轻球员，而不是替换他们。
senses.why: People, like seedlings, need support before they can stand; the verb transfers the gardener's role to a mentor.
senses.whyCN: 人如幼苗，站稳之前需要支撑；这个动词把园丁的角色移交给师长。

senses.title: Refine the mind
senses.definition: to improve a person's taste, manners or understanding through education and good company
senses.definitionCN: 通过教育与良好交往提升某人的趣味、举止或见识
senses.example: Travel and reading cultivate the mind.
senses.exampleCN: 旅行与阅读修养心智。
senses.why: The soil being improved is now internal, and the crop is judgment rather than food.
senses.whyCN: 此时被改良的土壤已转向内部，作物也变成判断力而非食物。

senses.title: Cultivate a useful contact
senses.definition: to seek and keep the favour of someone useful, often with an instrumental purpose
senses.definitionCN: 寻求并维持有用之人的好感，常带有工具性目的
senses.example: The lobbyist cultivates the committee chair.
senses.exampleCN: 说客刻意结交委员会主席。
senses.why: This sense exposes the metaphor's cold edge: a relationship can be grown for harvest rather than for itself.
senses.whyCN: 这一义显出比喻冷峻的一面：关系也可以为了收获而被栽培，而非为了它本身。

intro.en: Cultivate comes from Medieval Latin cultivare, to till, built on cultiva, tilled land, which in turn rests on cultus, the past participle of colere. It entered English through French in the sixteenth century. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultivate 来自中世纪拉丁 cultivare「耕作」，其基础是 cultiva「耕过的土地」，而 cultiva 又源于 colere 的过去分词 cultus。它在十六世纪经法语进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cultiva was the Medieval Latin name for land that had been worked, formed from cultus, the participle of colere.
items.cn: cultiva 是中世纪拉丁语对已耕作土地的称呼，由 colere 的分词 cultus 构成。

items.en: From cultiva came cultivare, a new verb meaning to till or to tend, built on an old participle rather than on a classical verb.
items.cn: 由 cultiva 产生 cultivare，这个新动词意为耕作或照管，它建在旧分词上，而非建在古典动词上。

items.en: Old French cultiver carried the verb towards English, and the English form cultivate is recorded from the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 cultiver 把这个动词带向英语，英语形式 cultivate 在十六世纪已有记录。

items.en: The earliest English uses are agricultural and concern the working of land and the raising of crops.
items.cn: 最早的英语用例属农业语境，涉及土地耕作与作物种植。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the verb was applied to the mind, manners and friendships, and by the nineteenth to bacteria in a medium.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个动词已用于心智、举止与友谊；到十九世纪又用于培养基中的细菌。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date and route): the exact French dialect path is not fully documented, and the earliest English citation is dated only approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代与路径）：经法语各方言的具体路径缺乏完整记载，英语最早书证的年代也只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same root that name neighbouring practices; group two holds general verbs for raising plants or helping growth.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该词根、指相邻实践的词；第二组是表示「种植」或「助长」的普通动词。

entries.definition: The noun for a way of life or a growth medium; it does not name the farmer's action.
entries.definitionCN: 指生活方式或培养基的名词，不指农人的动作。

entries.definition: The whole science and business of farming; cultivate names one action inside it.
entries.definitionCN: 农业的科学与产业整体；cultivate 只指其中的一个动作。

entries.definition: The branch of farming concerned with garden plants; cultivate is the verb that does the work.
entries.definitionCN: 农业中负责园艺植物的分支；cultivate 是执行这项工作的动词。

entries.definition: A religious system or devoted following from Latin cultus; it shares the root but not the agricultural sense.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 cultus 的宗教体系或狂热追随；共享词根，但不含农业义。

entries.definition: To manage a farm as a whole, including animals and equipment; cultivate concerns the soil and plants.
entries.definitionCN: 经营整个农场，包括动物与设备；cultivate 只关注土壤与植物。

entries.definition: To work the soil mechanically before sowing; it stops short of growing or caring for the crop.
entries.definitionCN: 播种前对土壤进行机械作业；不涉及作物生长或照管。

entries.definition: To care for something as it grows, often a child or talent; it stresses affection more than technique.
entries.definitionCN: 在生长过程中照料，常指孩子或才能；比技术更强调情感。

entries.definition: To encourage the development of an idea, skill or relationship; it is the abstract cousin of cultivate.
entries.definitionCN: 鼓励想法、技能或关系的发展；是 cultivate 的抽象近亲。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cultiva 'tilled land' plus -ate 'to make': to make land tilled, then to make anything grow.
normal.cn: cultiva「耕过的土地」加 -ate「使……」：使土地被耕，再使任何东西生长。

normal.en: The family runs cultivate, cultivation, cultivator, cultivable, cultivar, cultivated.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cultivate、cultivation、cultivator、cultivable、cultivar、cultivated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the split: cultivate land, cultivate bacteria, cultivate a habit.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示分工：耕种土地、培养细菌、养成习惯。

normal.en: The object tells you the sense: soil, plants, microbes, skills, people or contacts.
normal.cn: 看宾语就能判断义项：土壤、植物、微生物、技能、人或人脉。

normal.en: The phrase cultivate a taste for marks the acquired, learned sense.
normal.cn: 短语「培养对……的爱好」标出后天习得的那一层。

abstract.en: Picture a hand that keeps breaking the same small patch of earth until it is soft enough to receive seed.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手反复翻同一小块土，直到它松软得可以接住种子。

abstract.en: Picture a mentor who prunes a student's bad habits as a gardener prunes a vine.
abstract.cn: 想象一位师长修剪学生的坏习惯，如同园丁修剪藤蔓。

abstract.en: Picture a contact list tended like a herb bed, each name watered on a schedule.
abstract.cn: 想象一份人脉名单被当作香草床照料，每个名字都按日程浇水。

examples.en: Farmers cultivate the terraces by hand because machines cannot reach them.
examples.cn: 农民手工耕作梯田，因为机器上不去。

examples.en: The team cultivates a rare fungus that breaks down plastic.
examples.cn: 这个团队培养一种能分解塑料的稀有真菌。

examples.en: Good managers cultivate the people who will replace them.
examples.cn: 好的管理者会培养将来接替自己的人。

dict_mnemonic.text: cult（耕种、培育）+ -ivate（使动）→ 让土地长出作物，也让才能、习惯与关系长起来。

root: 中世纪拉丁 cultiva「耕过的土地」→ cultivare「耕作」→ 法语 cultiver → 英语 cultivate；更早可追到 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」，其印欧词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one verb: a patch of ground is worked, then the same working is applied to plants, microbes, habits, friendships, pupils, minds and useful contacts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动词展开：先耕一块地，再把同一种劳作用于植物、微生物、习惯、友谊、学生、心智与有用的人脉。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand returns to the same patch of soil each season, and the soil answers with a little more growth each time.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手每个季节都回到同一块地，土地每次都以多一点生长来回应。

branches.en: THE PLOT: open field first, then the smaller plot of a garden.
branches.cn: 地块：先是开阔的田，再是园子里更小的一块。

branches.en: THE DISH: a contained medium repeats the field on a microscopic scale.
branches.cn: 培养皿：围住的培养基在微观尺度上重复了田地。

branches.en: THE HABIT: repetition is the water that keeps an ability alive.
branches.cn: 习惯：重复就是让能力存活的水。

branches.en: THE PEOPLE: friendship and mentorship both require scheduled attention.
branches.cn: 人：友谊与师徒关系都需要按时的关注。

branches.en: THE MIND AND THE CONTACT: inward refinement and outward networking use the same verb.
branches.cn: 心智与人脉：向内的修养与向外的结交使用同一个动词。

intro.en: Cultivate is a Latin-derived verb whose root and suffixes also build the rest of its English family, so each part can be read separately.
intro.cn: cultivate 是拉丁来源的动词，其词根与后缀还构成英语词族的其余部分，因此每一部分都可单独读出。

latinIntro.en: Latin cultiva and cultivare supply the verb; -ate marks the action, while -ation, -or, -able and -ar build the related nouns and adjectives.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cultiva 与 cultivare 提供动词；-ate 标记动作，而 -ation、-or、-able 与 -ar 构成相关名词与形容词。

items.example: The noun named the ground before the verb named the work.
items.exampleCN: 先有指土地的名词，才有指工作的动词。

items.example: The verb spread through French into English.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词经法语传入英语。

items.example: They cultivate the lower field.
items.exampleCN: 他们耕种低处的田。

items.example: The ending turns the noun stem into an action.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把名词词干变成动作。

items.meaning: the work of tilling or tending
items.example: Cultivation of the slope took three years.
items.exampleCN: 这块坡地的耕作花了三年。

items.structure: cultivate + -or (one who acts or a tool)
items.meaning: a tiller or a cultivating machine
items.example: The cultivator broke the crust between rows.
items.exampleCN: 中耕机打碎了行间的硬壳。

items.meaning: able to be tilled or grown
items.example: The plateau is barely cultivable.
items.exampleCN: 这片高原几乎无法耕种。

items.example: The cultivar was bred for dry soil.
items.exampleCN: 这个品种是为旱地培育的。

items.example: The cultivated man spoke last.
items.exampleCN: 那位有教养的男士最后发言。

latinEntries.structure: cultivare, cultivavi, cultivatum (verb, first conjugation, Medieval Latin)

definition_zh: 耕作的；人工栽培的；（人）有教养的；后天培养出来的
definition_en: (of land) prepared and used for crops; (of plants or organisms) grown under human control; (of a person, taste or skill) developed by deliberate training
core_image: 一块行距笔直的田，作物比野地里的同类更壮；田边站着一位举止从容、说话有分寸的人
scene: 田里的行距被绳子量得笔直，苗高一致，杂草清得干净，主人说话轻缓而有分寸。The cultivated field yields more than the wild plot beside it.
sceneCN: 这里指「经人工耕作与照管的」（第 1 个义项：耕地）；句意为这块耕作过的田比旁边的荒地收成更多。

pos.zh: 耕作的；人工栽培的；有教养的；后天培养的

derivatives.zh: cultivate + -ation（动作或结果）→ 耕作；培养
cultivate + -or（施动者或工具）→ 耕作的人；中耕机
cultivate + -able（能……的）→ 可耕种的
cultivate + -ar（园艺名词后缀）→ 栽培品种
un-（否定）+ cultivated → 未开垦的；未受教育的
re-（重新）+ cultivated → 休耕后重新耕作的

senses.title: Land that has been tilled
senses.definition: describing land that has been broken, worked and used for crops rather than left wild
senses.definitionCN: 描述经过翻耕、整治并用于种植作物、而非任其荒芜的土地
senses.example: Cultivated land stops where the slope becomes too steep.
senses.exampleCN: 耕地到坡度过陡处为止。
senses.why: The past participle of cultivate turns the action into a state, so land carries the mark of having been worked.
senses.whyCN: cultivate 的过去分词把动作转为状态，因此土地带着「已被耕作」的印记。

senses.title: Field crops grown on purpose
senses.titleCN: 有目的种植的田间作物
senses.definition: describing crops that people have planted and tended in fields, as opposed to wild plants
senses.definitionCN: 描述人们种在田里并加以照管的作物，与野生植物相对
senses.example: Cultivated wheat shatters less easily than its wild ancestor.
senses.exampleCN: 栽培小麦比其野生祖先更不易落粒。
senses.why: Once a plant depends on people for sowing and weeding, it is described by the participle of the care it receives.
senses.whyCN: 一旦植物依赖人播种与除草，就用它所受照管的分词来描述。

senses.title: Garden plants from chosen stock
senses.titleCN: 由选育种苗栽培的园艺植物
senses.definition: describing ornamental or fruit plants raised from selected stock in a garden or nursery
senses.definitionCN: 描述在园圃或苗圃中由选育种苗育成的观赏或果树植物
senses.example: The cultivated rose has lost the scent of the wild briar.
senses.exampleCN: 栽培玫瑰已失去野蔷薇的香气。
senses.why: Garden plants are the clearest case of human choice: the stock itself, not only the soil, has been selected.
senses.whyCN: 园艺植物是人类选择最清楚的例子：被选的不仅是土壤，还有种苗本身。

senses.title: Grown in a laboratory medium
senses.titleCN: 在实验室培养基中培养的
senses.definition: describing microorganisms or cells grown under controlled laboratory conditions
senses.definitionCN: 描述在受控实验室条件下培养的微生物或细胞
senses.example: Cultivated cells behave differently from cells taken straight from tissue.
senses.exampleCN: 培养细胞的行为与直接从组织取出的细胞不同。
senses.why: Laboratory growth is deliberate cultivation, so the participle marks anything raised in a dish rather than in a body.
senses.whyCN: 实验室培养是有意的培育，因此这个分词标记一切在培养皿而非体内长成的东西。

senses.title: A person polished by education
senses.titleCN: 受过教育而举止得体的人
senses.definition: describing a person whose manners, speech and judgment have been refined by education and good company
senses.definitionCN: 描述举止、言谈与判断经教育与良好交往而变得优雅的人
senses.example: He was a cultivated man who never raised his voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他是一位有教养的男士，从不提高嗓门。
senses.why: The agricultural metaphor turns social: a person, like a garden, can be tended into a better shape.
senses.whyCN: 农业比喻转向社会：人如园子，可以被照料成更好的形状。

senses.title: A taste acquired by exposure
senses.definition: describing an appreciation that has been learned through repeated exposure rather than possessed naturally
senses.definitionCN: 描述经反复接触而学会、而非天生拥有的鉴赏力
senses.example: Her cultivated taste for opera began with film scores.
senses.exampleCN: 她对歌剧的后天品味始于电影配乐。
senses.why: Taste is not planted in a person at birth; it is grown by exposure, which is why the participle fits.
senses.whyCN: 品味并非与生俱来，而是靠接触长成，因此适合用这个分词。

senses.title: A skill built by training
senses.definition: describing an ability developed through deliberate practice rather than given by nature
senses.definitionCN: 描述经刻意练习发展出来、而非天赋所赐的能力
senses.example: His cultivated voice carried across the hall without strain.
senses.exampleCN: 他训练有素的嗓音毫不费力地传遍大厅。
senses.why: The contrast with native gifts is the point: what is cultivated was not there to begin with.
senses.whyCN: 与天赋的对照正是要点：被培养出来的东西起初并不存在。

senses.title: A relationship kept up on purpose
senses.definition: describing a friendship or contact that is deliberately maintained over time
senses.definitionCN: 描述长期被有意维持的友谊或人脉
senses.example: Their cultivated ties survived two changes of government.
senses.exampleCN: 他们经营的关系挺过了两次政府更替。
senses.why: A tie that is kept up is literally cultivated, and the participle records the effort behind its survival.
senses.whyCN: 被维持的关系确实是「被栽培」的，这个分词记录了它存活背后的投入。

intro.en: Cultivated is the past participle of cultivate used as an adjective. The verb came from Medieval Latin cultivare, and the adjectival use is recorded from the sixteenth century, with the social sense following in the eighteenth. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cultivated 是 cultivate 的过去分词作形容词。这个动词来自中世纪拉丁 cultivare，形容词用法在十六世纪已有记录，社会义则在十八世纪出现。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cultivare meant to till or tend; its past participle cultivatus supplied the form that English turned into an adjective.
items.cn: cultivare 意为耕作或照管；其过去分词 cultivatus 提供了英语转化为形容词的形式。

items.en: The first English adjectival uses describe land and plants that have been worked, keeping close to the participle's literal force.
items.cn: 最早的英语形容词用法描述被耕作过的土地与植物，贴近分词的字面力量。

items.en: Enlightenment writing applied the word to people, manners and taste, so a cultivated man became one whose mind had been tended.
items.cn: 启蒙时期的写作把这个词用于人、举止与品味，于是有教养的人成了心智受过照料的人。

items.en: Microbiology adopted the participle for organisms grown in a medium, giving the word a second technical life.
items.cn: 微生物学采用这个分词指在培养基中生长的生物，使这个词获得第二种技术生命。

items.en: Modern English keeps both readings side by side: cultivated land and a cultivated accent, one literal and one figurative.
items.cn: 现代英语把两种读法并置：耕作的田地与有教养的口音，一为字面，一为比喻。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): dictionaries date the adjectival use only approximately, and the exact path from agricultural to social meaning is not documented in detail.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：辞书对形容词用法的年代只有约数，从农业义到社会义的具体路径也缺乏详细记载。

note.en: Group one holds participles and adjectives from the same root that are easily swapped; group two holds adjectives for a polished or trained person or thing.
note.cn: 第一组是同出该词根、极易互换的分词与形容词；第二组是描述「被磨得精致、受过训练」的人或物的形容词。

entries.definition: From culture, not cultivate: it can mean refined in manners or grown in a medium, as in cultured pearls.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 culture 而非 cultivate：既可指举止优雅，也可指在培养基中生长，如养殖珍珠。

entries.definition: The plain opposite: land never worked, or a person without training; it denies the participle rather than naming a new quality.
entries.definitionCN: 直接的反义：从未耕作的土地，或未受训练的人；它否定该分词，而不命名新性质。

entries.definition: Able to be cultivated, whether or not it actually is; cultivated land has already been worked.
entries.definitionCN: 能够被耕作，无论实际是否已耕；而 cultivated 的土地已经耕过。

entries.definition: The noun for a way of life or a growth medium; it names the field, while cultivated describes what came out of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指生活方式或培养基的名词；它命名场域，而 cultivated 描述从中产生的结果。

entries.definition: Purified or made elegant by taking away what is coarse; cultivated stresses the care that grew the quality, refined stresses the removal of roughness.
entries.definitionCN: 通过去除粗劣部分而变得纯净或优雅；cultivated 强调培育出该品质的照料，refined 强调去除粗糙。

entries.definition: Having received formal instruction; cultivated is broader and includes manners and taste acquired outside school.
entries.definitionCN: 受过正式教育；cultivated 范围更广，包含在校外获得的举止与品味。

entries.definition: Made manageable by domestication; it applies to animals and wildness, not to land care or personal polish.
entries.definitionCN: 通过驯化而变得可控；适用于动物与野性，不用于土地照料或个人修养。

entries.definition: Carefully prepared for a particular role or appearance; cultivated can be wider and less career-directed.
entries.definitionCN: 为特定角色或外表精心准备；cultivated 可以更宽，未必指向职业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: cultivate plus -ed: the action is finished, and what remains is a state.
normal.cn: cultivate 加 -ed：动作已完成，留下的是状态。

normal.en: The family runs cultivate, cultivation, cultivator, cultivable, cultivar, cultivated.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cultivate、cultivation、cultivator、cultivable、cultivar、cultivated。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: cultivated land, cultivated plants, a cultivated man.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：耕地、栽培植物、有教养的人。

normal.en: The laboratory says cultivated cells; the garden says cultivated roses.
normal.cn: 实验室说培养细胞，园子说栽培玫瑰。

normal.en: The contrast is always with wild, native or untrained.
normal.cn: 它的对照项总是野生、天生或未受训练。

abstract.en: Picture a field whose straight rows are themselves a record of years of decisions.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田，笔直的行距本身就是多年决断的记录。

abstract.en: Picture a voice that has been sanded smooth by decades of practice.
abstract.cn: 想象一副被数十年练习打磨光滑的嗓音。

abstract.en: Picture a friendship with visible stitching, mended each time it frayed.
abstract.cn: 想象一段带着明显针脚、每次磨损都被补好的友谊。

examples.en: The cultivated slope supports three crops a year, while the wild one supports none.
examples.cn: 这块被耕作的坡地一年能种三季，而荒地一季也没有。

examples.en: Cultivated mushrooms are grown on sterilised straw.
examples.cn: 栽培蘑菇种在消过毒的秸秆上。

examples.en: His cultivated manner made even bad news easier to hear.
examples.cn: 他有教养的举止让坏消息也变得容易听进去。

dict_mnemonic.text: cultivate（耕作、培养）+ -ed（已完成）→ 已被耕过的、已被培养成的；土地、植物、细胞、人与品味都能用。

root: cultivate + -ed；cultivate 来自中世纪拉丁 cultivare「耕作」，再上溯 cultiva「耕过的土地」与 colere「耕作、居住、敬奉」，更早词根属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one participle: what people have worked on carries the mark of that work, whether it is soil, a crop, a cell, a person, a taste, a skill or a tie.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个分词展开：凡被人经手照料过的东西都带着那份劳作的印记，无论是土壤、作物、细胞、人、品味、技能还是关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a field with straight rows and a person with measured speech are both surfaces that show the marks of long care.
core.cn: 核心意象：行距笔直的田与说话有分寸的人，都是显示出长期照料痕迹的表面。

branches.en: THE GROUND: the participle's oldest and most literal use.
branches.cn: 土地：这个分词最古老、最字面的用法。

branches.en: THE PLANTS: field crops and garden stock, both chosen and tended by people.
branches.cn: 植物：田间作物与园中种苗，都由人选择并照料。

branches.en: THE DISH: laboratory growth is cultivation made visible under glass.
branches.cn: 培养皿：实验室里的生长是隔着玻璃可见的培育。

branches.en: THE PERSON AND THE SKILL: polish of manner and training of ability.
branches.cn: 人与技能：举止的优雅与能力的训练。

branches.en: TASTE AND TIES: both are acquired slowly and kept by repetition.
branches.cn: 品味与关系：两者都缓慢获得，并靠重复维持。

intro.en: Cultivated is a participle-adjective, so its parts are the verb cultivate and the ending -ed, with the rest of the family built from the same root.
intro.cn: cultivated 是分词形容词，其组成部分是动词 cultivate 与词尾 -ed，词族其余成员也由同一词根构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin cultivare supplies the verb; the English ending -ed marks the completed state, while -ation, -or, -able and -ar build the related family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 cultivare 提供动词；英语词尾 -ed 标记完成状态，而 -ation、-or、-able 与 -ar 构成相关词族。

items.example: People cultivate the plant for its oil.
items.exampleCN: 人们为取其油而栽培这种植物。

items.example: The ending turns an action into a finished state.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把动作变成完成状态。

items.meaning: the work of tilling or tending
items.example: Cultivation began with the first ploughing.
items.exampleCN: 培育从第一次犁地开始。

items.structure: cultivate + -or (one who acts or a tool)
items.example: The cultivator passes between the rows.
items.exampleCN: 中耕机在行间穿行。

items.example: The cultivable strip is only ten metres wide.
items.exampleCN: 可耕种的地带只有十米宽。

items.example: Each cultivar ripens at a different time.
items.exampleCN: 每个品种的成熟时间都不同。

items.example: Uncultivated ground held the old wildflowers.
items.exampleCN: 未开垦的地里留着旧日的野花。

items.example: The recultivated strip yielded a poor first crop.
items.exampleCN: 重新耕作的地带第一季收成很差。

latinEntries.structure: cultivare, cultivavi, cultivatum (verb, first conjugation, Medieval Latin)

definition_zh: 收获；收割；收成；（努力得到的）成果；采集（数据、细胞、野生资源）
definition_en: the act or season of gathering ripe crops, the crop gathered, the result of effort, or the act of collecting resources
core_image: 一片成熟麦田在短时间内被割倒、捆扎、装车，田里只剩整齐的茬
scene: 麦穗低下头，镰刀从田边推进，捆好的束子一列列码在车上，天色已近黄昏。The harvest must be brought in before the first storm.
sceneCN: 这里指「把成熟作物收回来」（第 1 个义项：收割庄稼）；句意为必须在第一场暴风雨前完成收获。

pos.zh: 收获；收割；收成；（努力的）成果
收割；采集（数据、细胞、野生资源）

derivatives.zh: harvest + -er（施动者或工具）→ 收割的人；收割机
harvest + -ing（动作名词）→ 收割作业；采集
harvest + -ed（过去分词作形容词）→ 已收割的
harvest + -able（能……的）→ 可收割的；可采集的
post-（之后）+ harvest → 收获后的（语义偏移：指采收之后的处理与储藏）
pre-（之前）+ harvest → 收获前的（语义偏移：指采收之前的田间管理）
harvest + man（人）→ 收割者；盲蛛（语义偏移：一种外形像长腿收割者的蛛形动物）

senses.title: Cut and gather ripe crops
senses.definition: to cut, pick or dig up ripe crops and bring them in
senses.definitionCN: 把成熟作物割下、摘下或挖出并运回
senses.example: They harvest the wheat before the rain breaks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在雨来之前收割小麦。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the decisive act of the farming year: what has grown is finally taken.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是农事年里决定性的动作：长成的东西终于被取走。

senses.title: The act or season of gathering
senses.definition: the work or the time of gathering crops, as in a late harvest
senses.definitionCN: 收集作物的劳作或时段，如晚收
senses.example: The harvest lasted three weeks that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年的收获持续了三个星期。
senses.why: English often turns a season and its main activity into one noun, and harvest names both at once.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一个季节与其主要活动合成一个名词，harvest 同时指两者。

senses.title: The crop that is gathered
senses.definition: the amount of crop produced and gathered in one season
senses.definitionCN: 一季中产出并收上来的作物总量
senses.example: A dry summer cut the harvest by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱的夏天使收成减少了三分之一。
senses.why: By metonymy the act becomes the thing it produces, so people speak of a good or bad harvest.
senses.whyCN: 以转喻方式，行为变成它的产物，于是人们说收成好或坏。

senses.title: The fruit of long effort
senses.definition: the result or reward that comes from sustained work, as in the harvest of years of research
senses.definitionCN: 持续工作带来的结果或回报，如多年研究的成果
senses.example: The book was the harvest of ten quiet years.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是十年静默工作的成果。
senses.why: The agricultural image generalizes: any long investment eventually has a gathering time.
senses.whyCN: 农业意象被一般化：任何长期投入最终都有采收的时候。

senses.title: Collect data in bulk
senses.definition: to gather large amounts of data or information, often automatically
senses.definitionCN: 大量收集数据或信息，常为自动进行
senses.example: The app harvests location data from every user.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用从每位用户那里采集位置数据。
senses.why: Data is treated as a crop: it is already there, and the work is to gather it efficiently.
senses.whyCN: 数据被当作作物：它已经在那里，工作就是高效地把它收上来。

senses.title: Take cells or organs for use
senses.titleCN: 摘取细胞或器官供使用
senses.definition: to remove cells, tissue or organs from a body for medical treatment or research
senses.definitionCN: 从身体中取出细胞、组织或器官，用于治疗或研究
senses.example: Surgeons harvested a nerve from the patient's leg.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生从病人腿部取出一段神经。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the image of taking a living supply from where it grew.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了「从生长处取走活材料」的意象。

senses.title: Gather wild resources
senses.definition: to gather wild plants, shellfish or timber from their natural setting
senses.definitionCN: 从自然环境中采集野生植物、贝类或木材
senses.example: Villagers harvest shellfish at the low tide.
senses.exampleCN: 村民在退潮时采拾贝类。
senses.why: Not everything gathered is planted; the word also covers taking what the wild has produced.
senses.whyCN: 被收走的不都是种下的；这个词也涵盖取走野生环境产出之物。

senses.title: Autumn as the old season word
senses.definition: the season of autumn, the original meaning of the word in Old English
senses.definitionCN: 秋天这一季节，即该词在古英语中的本义
senses.example: In older texts harvest names the season, not only its work.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的文本里，这个词指季节本身，而不只是季节里的活。
senses.why: Old English hærfest meant autumn; the modern crop sense narrowed out of the season when crops were cut.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hærfest 意为秋天；现代作物义是从「收割作物的季节」中收窄出来的。

intro.en: Harvest goes back to Old English hærfest, autumn, from Proto-Germanic harbitas. The same word family survives as German Herbst, autumn. The crop sense narrowed out of the season sense. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: harvest 可上溯到古英语 hærfest「秋天」，源自原始日耳曼语 harbitas。同族词在德语中保留为 Herbst「秋天」。作物义是从季节义中收窄出来的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hærfest named autumn and also the gathering of crops that filled that season; the two readings were not separated.
items.cn: hærfest 指秋天，也指填满这个季节的收作物；两种读法尚未分开。

items.en: The Germanic form harbitas is reconstructed from the older English and German evidence; it is not directly recorded.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 harbitas 是由较早的英语与德语证据重构出来的，并未被直接记录。

items.en: The word is generally connected with a root meaning to gather or pluck, but the exact Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 这个词一般认为与表示「收集、采摘」的词根有关，但确切的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Middle English kept both autumn and crop readings, while the season sense slowly passed to the Latin-derived word autumn.
items.cn: 中古英语同时保留「秋天」与「作物」两种读法，而季节义慢慢转给拉丁来源的 autumn。

items.en: The verb harvest appears later than the noun and extends the gathering image to data, organs and wild resources.
items.cn: 动词 harvest 比名词出现得晚，并把采集意象扩展到数据、器官与野生资源。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Germanic origin is reconstructed only, and no single Indo-European source is agreed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：日耳曼语之前的来源只有重构形式，学界并未达成单一印欧来源。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to harvest but name different things; group two holds words for taking in what has grown.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近 harvest、却指不同事物的词；第二组是表示「把长成之物收进来」的词。

entries.definition: The modern season word, borrowed from Latin autumnus; it replaced the season sense of harvest but is not related to it.
entries.definitionCN: 现代的季节词，借自拉丁 autumnus；它取代了 harvest 的季节义，但与之并非同源。

entries.definition: One who harvests or a machine that cuts and threshes grain; it is the doer, not the crop or the season.
entries.definitionCN: 收割的人或收割脱粒的机器；它是施动者，不是作物或季节。

entries.definition: A long-legged arachnid, named for its resemblance to a reaper; it is not a person who works in the fields.
entries.definitionCN: 一种长腿蛛形动物，因形似收割者而得名；并不是在田里劳作的人。

entries.definition: A celebration held after the crop is in; it marks the end of harvesting rather than the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 庄稼收完后举行的庆祝；它标记收割结束，而非收割本身。

entries.definition: A plant or plant product grown in quantity; the harvest is the act of taking it in, or its total yield.
entries.definitionCN: 大量种植的植物或植物产品；harvest 是把它收进来的动作，或总产量。

entries.definition: The amount produced by land or by an effort; it is a quantity, while harvest can be the work, the season or the crop.
entries.definitionCN: 土地或努力产出的数量；它是量，而 harvest 可以是工作、季节或作物。

entries.definition: To cut grain by hand or machine; it is the first step of harvesting and does not cover data or organs.
entries.definitionCN: 用手或机器割谷；是收获的第一步，不涵盖数据或器官。

entries.definition: The general verb for bringing scattered things together; harvest is more specific and implies a crop ready to be taken.
entries.definitionCN: 把散落之物聚拢的普通动词；harvest 更具体，暗示作物已到可收之时。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English hærfest meant autumn: the season and its work were one word.
normal.cn: 古英语 hærfest 意为秋天：季节与季节里的活曾是同一个词。

normal.en: The family runs harvest, harvesting, harvester, harvested, harvestable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 harvest、harvesting、harvester、harvested、harvestable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: bring in the harvest, harvest season, harvest festival.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出田间义：把庄稼收回来、收获季节、丰收节。

normal.en: The modern verb extends to data, organs, rainwater and shellfish.
normal.cn: 现代动词扩展到数据、器官、雨水与贝类。

normal.en: German Herbst still means autumn, the lost sense of the English word.
normal.cn: 德语 Herbst 仍指秋天，正是英语这个词丢失的义项。

abstract.en: Picture a field that disappears into stacks and sacks in a single afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田在一个下午里消失，变成一堆堆捆束与一袋袋粮食。

abstract.en: Picture a decade of notes finally tied into one bundle.
abstract.cn: 想象十年的笔记终于被扎成一捆。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pool emptied at low water, every shellfish taken before the sea returns.
abstract.cn: 想象退潮后的潮池被掏空，海水回来之前每一只贝都被取走。

examples.en: The combine harvested the field in two days.
examples.cn: 联合收割机两天就收完了这块田。

examples.en: This year's harvest was the smallest in a decade.
examples.cn: 今年的收成是十年来最少的。

examples.en: Researchers harvest tissue samples from consenting patients.
examples.cn: 研究人员从知情同意的病人身上采集组织样本。

dict_mnemonic.text: harvest 本指秋天，后来专指秋天里最要紧的活——把长熟的东西收回来；于是作物、收成、成果、数据都能「收」。

root: 古英语 hærfest「秋天」，源自原始日耳曼 harbitas；一般认为与表示「收集、采摘」的词根有关，但更早的印欧形式属重构。德语 Herbst「秋天」为同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one moment: ripe growth is cut and carried in, and that moment then becomes a season, a yield, a reward and a way of collecting anything useful.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个时刻展开：成熟之物被割下并运回，这个时刻随后变成季节、产量、回报，以及收集任何有用之物的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ripe field is emptied in a short, decisive burst of work, and the year's growth becomes a store.
core.cn: 核心意象：成熟的田在一阵短促而决定性的劳作中被收空，一年的生长变成一座粮仓。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS TIME: cutting the crop and the weeks in which it is done.
branches.cn: 动作与其时间：割下作物，以及做这件事的那几周。

branches.en: THE SEASON AND ITS STORE: autumn and the amount it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 季节与其储藏：秋天，以及它留下的数量。

branches.en: THE REWARD: any long effort has a gathering day.
branches.cn: 回报：任何长期投入都有采收的一天。

branches.en: THE DATA FIELD: information is gathered like grain.
branches.cn: 数据之田：信息像谷物一样被收走。

branches.en: THE LIVING SUPPLY: cells, organs, shellfish and timber are taken from where they grew.
branches.cn: 活的供应：细胞、器官、贝类与木材都从生长处取走。

intro.en: Harvest is a native Germanic word, not a Latin derivative; its English family is built with ordinary suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: harvest 是日耳曼本族词，并非拉丁派生词；它的英语词族由普通后缀与复合方式构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin relative exists for this word, so the Latin side is left empty; the family is entirely Germanic and English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁部分留空；其词族完全属于日耳曼语与英语。

items.example: The noun once named the whole season.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词曾命名整个季节。

items.meaning: one who does, or a tool that does
items.example: The suffix builds harvester from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由动词构成 harvester。

items.meaning: a reaper or a harvesting machine
items.example: The harvester cleared the last row at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 收割机在黄昏清完了最后一行。

items.example: Harvesting began before sunrise.
items.exampleCN: 收割在天亮前开始。

items.example: The harvested grain was dried on racks.
items.exampleCN: 收下的谷子在架子上晾干。

items.meaning: ready or able to be gathered
items.example: Only half the stand was harvestable.
items.exampleCN: 只有一半的林分可采伐。

items.example: Postharvest losses were cut by better storage.
items.exampleCN: 更好的储藏减少了收获后的损失。

items.example: Preharvest checks look for mould.
items.exampleCN: 收获前检查寻找霉变。

items.meaning: a reaper; also a long-legged arachnid
items.example: A harvestman crossed the stubble.
items.exampleCN: 一只盲蛛爬过茬地。

definition_zh: 收割；收获（作业）；采集（数据、细胞、雨水、木材等）
definition_en: the activity of gathering a crop, or of collecting data, cells, water or wild resources
core_image: 收割机在田里来回，粮仓口不断落下的谷粒堆成小山
scene: 收割机沿田边转圈，脱粒后的谷粒从管道落进拖车，司机盯着满仓指示灯。Harvesting continues until the field is bare.
sceneCN: 这里指「收割这一持续进行的作业」（第 1 个义项）；句意为收割作业一直持续到田里收空。

derivatives.zh: harvest + -er（施动者或工具）→ 收割的人；收割机
harvest + -ed（过去分词）→ 已收割的
harvest + -able（能……的）→ 可收割的
post-（之后）+ harvest → 收获后的
pre-（之前）+ harvest → 收获前的
harvest + man → 收割者；盲蛛

senses.title: The work of cutting and gathering
senses.definition: the ongoing work of cutting, picking and gathering a ripe crop
senses.definitionCN: 把成熟作物割下、摘下并收拢的持续工作
senses.example: Harvesting begins when the grain is hard enough to snap.
senses.exampleCN: 谷粒硬到能掰断时，收割就开始了。
senses.why: The -ing form names the activity as it happens rather than the single decisive act.
senses.whyCN: -ing 形式命名正在进行的活动，而非单个决定性动作。

senses.title: The period of the work
senses.definition: the span of days or weeks during which the crop is gathered
senses.definitionCN: 收作物所用的数日或数周时间
senses.example: Harvesting overlaps with the start of the school year.
senses.exampleCN: 收割期与开学时间重叠。
senses.why: A season is defined by the activity that fills it, so the -ing noun can name the period too.
senses.whyCN: 季节由填满它的活动定义，因此这个 -ing 名词也能指该时段。

senses.title: Mechanical harvesting
senses.definition: gathering crops with combines, binders or other machines
senses.definitionCN: 用联合收割机、割捆机或其他机器收集作物
senses.example: Mechanical harvesting leaves less stubble for grazing.
senses.exampleCN: 机械收割留下的茬口较少，不利于放牧。
senses.why: Once machines take over the work, the activity splits by means rather than by purpose.
senses.whyCN: 机器接手后，这项活动按手段而非目的分化。

senses.title: Hand harvesting
senses.definition: gathering crops by hand, often for delicate or selective work
senses.definitionCN: 用手收集作物，常用于精细或选择性作业
senses.example: Hand harvesting protects the fruit from bruising.
senses.exampleCN: 人工采收保护果实不被碰伤。
senses.why: The same activity is contrasted with machines because the hand can choose and spare what steel cannot.
senses.whyCN: 同一活动与机器对照，因为手能挑选并保护钢铁做不到的东西。

senses.title: Automated data collection
senses.definition: the systematic or automatic gathering of data from users, sensors or records
senses.definitionCN: 从用户、传感器或记录中系统性或自动地收集数据
senses.example: Data harvesting happens every time the page loads.
senses.exampleCN: 页面每次加载都会发生数据采集。
senses.why: The crop image survives in digital form: information is already growing somewhere and is taken in bulk.
senses.whyCN: 作物意象以数字形式存活：信息已在某处生长，被大批取走。

senses.title: Removing cells or organs
senses.definition: the removal of cells, tissue or organs from a body for treatment, donation or research
senses.definitionCN: 从身体取出细胞、组织或器官，用于治疗、捐献或研究
senses.example: Organ harvesting must follow strict consent rules.
senses.exampleCN: 器官摘取必须遵守严格的同意规则。
senses.why: The medical activity keeps the literal image of taking a living supply at its peak.
senses.whyCN: 医学活动保留「在最佳时取走活材料」的字面意象。

senses.title: Collecting rainwater
senses.definition: the capture and storage of rainwater from roofs or catchments for later use
senses.definitionCN: 从屋顶或集水区收集并储存雨水以备后用
senses.example: Rainwater harvesting supplies the garden through dry months.
senses.exampleCN: 雨水收集在旱月里供给花园。
senses.why: What falls freely is treated as a crop to be caught rather than a resource to be pumped.
senses.whyCN: 自然落下之物被当作待收的作物，而非待抽取的资源。

senses.title: Taking timber or wild stock
senses.titleCN: 采伐木材或捕取野生资源
senses.definition: the gathering of timber, fish or wild plants from a managed or natural population
senses.definitionCN: 从经营或自然种群中采集木材、鱼类或野生植物
senses.example: Timber harvesting is limited to the winter months.
senses.exampleCN: 木材采伐仅限于冬季数月。
senses.why: The gathering image extends to any standing supply, whether planted or wild.
senses.whyCN: 采集意象扩展到任何现成储备，无论栽培还是野生。

intro.en: Harvesting is the verbal noun of harvest, formed with the native English suffix -ing. The base word goes back to Old English hærfest, autumn. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: harvesting 是 harvest 的动名词，由英语本族后缀 -ing 构成。其基础词可上溯到古英语 hærfest「秋天」。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hærfest named autumn and the gathering that filled it, so the later activity noun had a season already built into it.
items.cn: hærfest 指秋天与填满秋天的收作物，因此后来的活动名词自带一个季节。

items.en: The suffix -ing turns a verb into the name of its ongoing activity, as in harvesting, planting and threshing.
items.cn: 后缀 -ing 把动词变成其持续活动的名称，如收割、种植与脱粒。

items.en: Middle English used harvesting for the work of the fields before the noun harvest narrowed to the crop and the season.
items.cn: 中古英语已用 harvesting 指田间的活，后来名词 harvest 才收窄到作物与季节。

items.en: Machine reaping in the nineteenth century made harvesting a distinct operation with its own schedules and equipment.
items.cn: 十九世纪的机械收割使 harvesting 成为有独立日程与设备的作业。

items.en: The twentieth and twenty-first centuries extended the word to data, organs, rainwater and timber.
items.cn: 二十与二十一世纪把这个词扩展到数据、器官、雨水与木材。

items.en: Source uncertain (base-word origin): the pre-Germanic root of harvest is reconstructed only, and the first use of the -ing noun is dated approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（基础词词源）：harvest 在日耳曼语之前的词根只有重构形式，这个 -ing 名词的首见年代也只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds forms and compounds that are easily mistaken for the activity; group two holds nouns for taking in what has grown.
note.cn: 第一组是易被误当成「这项活动」的词形与复合词；第二组是表示「把长成之物收进来」的名词。

entries.definition: The base noun names the crop, the season or one decisive act; harvesting stresses the work as a process.
entries.definitionCN: 基础名词指作物、季节或一次决定性动作；harvesting 强调作为过程的工作。

entries.definition: A person or machine that does the work; it is the agent, not the activity.
entries.definitionCN: 做这项工作的人或机器；它是施动者，不是活动。

entries.definition: A long-legged arachnid named for its reaper-like shape; it has nothing to do with farm labour.
entries.definitionCN: 因形似收割者而得名的长腿蛛形动物，与农活无关。

entries.definition: The celebration after the work is finished; it marks the end of harvesting, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 工作结束后的庆祝；它标记收割结束，而非过程本身。

entries.definition: The cutting of grain, the first stage of the work; harvesting also includes gathering and hauling.
entries.definitionCN: 割谷，是工作的第一阶段；harvesting 还包括收拢与运输。

entries.definition: The general act of bringing scattered things together; harvesting is crop-specific and seasonal.
entries.definitionCN: 把散落之物聚拢的一般行为；harvesting 特指作物且具季节性。

entries.definition: The organized taking of items or data; it is neutral in tone, while harvesting keeps the agricultural image.
entries.definitionCN: 有组织地取走物品或数据；语气中性，而 harvesting 保留农业意象。

entries.definition: The practice of taking crops from land, often repeatedly; it names the land use rather than the gathering operation.
entries.definitionCN: 从土地上获取作物的做法，常为反复进行；它命名土地利用，而非收集作业。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: harvest plus -ing: the work seen while it is still going on.
normal.cn: harvest 加 -ing：正在持续进行时被看到的工作。

normal.en: The family runs harvest, harvesting, harvester, harvested, harvestable.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 harvest、harvesting、harvester、harvested、harvestable。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the means: mechanical harvesting, hand harvesting.
normal.cn: 固定搭配按手段分工：机械收割、人工采收。

normal.en: The same -ing noun appears in data harvesting and rainwater harvesting.
normal.cn: 同一个 -ing 名词出现在数据采集与雨水收集中。

normal.en: The season phrase harvesting season shows that the activity can name a period.
normal.cn: 短语 harvesting season 表明这项活动也能指一段时间。

abstract.en: Picture a machine tracing the field in ever-smaller rectangles until nothing is left.
abstract.cn: 想象一台机器在田里绕出越来越小的矩形，直到什么都不剩。

abstract.en: Picture a roof quietly filling a tank all winter without anyone carrying a bucket.
abstract.cn: 想象整个冬天屋顶悄悄把水箱装满，没有人提桶。

abstract.en: Picture a webpage that takes a small sample of every visitor and stores it in a jar.
abstract.cn: 想象一个网页从每位访客身上取一小份样本，存进罐子里。

examples.en: Harvesting at night keeps the fruit cooler.
examples.cn: 夜间采收能让果实保持更低的温度。

examples.en: The company's data harvesting practices are under review.
examples.cn: 这家公司的数据采集做法正在接受审查。

examples.en: Rainwater harvesting reduced the farm's water bill.
examples.cn: 雨水收集降低了农场的水费。

dict_mnemonic.text: harvest（收割）+ -ing（进行中的事）→ 正在进行的收割；从麦田扩展到数据、器官、雨水与木材。

root: harvest + -ing；harvest 出自古英语 hærfest「秋天」，源自原始日耳曼 harbitas，更早的印欧来源属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one ongoing activity: a crop is taken in, and the same taking-in is applied to data, organs, rain and timber.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一项持续活动展开：先把作物收进来，再把同一种「收进来」用于数据、器官、雨水与木材。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a machine or a pair of hands moves across a ripe field, and the field behind it is empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：机器或一双手扫过成熟的田，身后的田已经空了。

branches.en: THE OPERATION AND ITS CALENDAR: the work and the weeks it occupies.
branches.cn: 作业与其日历：这项工作以及它占据的几周。

branches.en: THE MEANS: steel or hands, each with its own advantage.
branches.cn: 手段：钢铁或双手，各有优势。

branches.en: THE DIGITAL CROP: browsing behaviour is taken in like grain.
branches.cn: 数字作物：浏览行为像谷物一样被收走。

branches.en: THE BODY: living tissue is removed at its peak.
branches.cn: 身体：活组织在最佳时被取出。

branches.en: THE STANDING SUPPLY: rain, timber and wild stock are gathered from what is already there.
branches.cn: 现成储备：雨水、木材与野生资源都从已有的东西中收集。

intro.en: Harvesting is a native Germanic base plus the English suffix -ing, so the word can be read as a process noun built from an old season word.
intro.cn: harvesting 是日耳曼本族基础词加英语后缀 -ing，因此可以读作由一个古老季节词构成的过程名词。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin relative exists for the base word, so the Latin side is left empty; the family is Germanic and English.
latinIntro.cn: 基础词没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁部分留空；其词族属于日耳曼语与英语。

items.example: The base noun still names the crop.
items.exampleCN: 基础名词仍指作物。

items.example: The suffix also builds planting and threshing.
items.exampleCN: 同一后缀还构成 planting 与 threshing。

items.example: Harvesting stopped when the rain came.
items.exampleCN: 下雨时收割停止了。

items.example: The harvester broke down at noon.
items.exampleCN: 收割机中午坏了。

items.example: The harvested rows were left to dry.
items.exampleCN: 收过的行被留在地里晾干。

items.example: The lower field is not yet harvestable.
items.exampleCN: 低处的田还不能收割。

items.example: Preharvest spraying is restricted.
items.exampleCN: 收获前的喷药受到限制。

items.example: Postharvest handling decides the final price.
items.exampleCN: 收获后的处理决定最终价格。

items.example: A harvestman sat on the gatepost.
items.exampleCN: 一只盲蛛停在门柱上。

definition_zh: 谷物；谷粒；颗粒；纹理；少量；（重量单位）格令
definition_en: a seed of a cereal plant, cereal crops collectively, a small hard particle, the pattern or direction of fibres, a very small amount, or a unit of weight
core_image: 掌心一小把金黄的谷粒，指缝间漏下几颗，木桌的纹路在旁边平行延伸
scene: 手掌摊开，几粒小麦从指缝滑落；旁边的旧木桌表面，细密的纹路顺着板面延伸。A single grain of sand can jam the whole mechanism.
sceneCN: 这里指「谷粒」（第 1 个义项：单粒种子）；句意为一粒沙子就能卡住整个机械。

pos.zh: 谷物；谷粒；颗粒；纹理；少量；格令（重量单位）

derivatives.zh: grain + -y（具有……性质的）→ 有颗粒感的（语义偏移：从单粒转为质地粗糙）
grainy + -ness（性质名词）→ 颗粒感
grain + -less（无……的）→ 无谷粒的；无纹理的
grain + -ed（具有……的）→ 有纹理的；成粒的
multi-（多）+ grain → 多谷物的（语义偏移：指混合多种谷物）
whole（完整）+ grain → 全谷物的（语义偏移：保留麸皮与胚芽）

senses.title: A single cereal seed
senses.definition: one seed of wheat, rice, maize or another cereal plant
senses.definitionCN: 小麦、稻、玉米或其他谷类植物的一粒种子
senses.example: Each grain must be dry before it is stored.
senses.exampleCN: 每一粒谷子在入仓前都必须干燥。
senses.why: The Latin source granum meant a seed, and the countable sense remains the most concrete one.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁来源 granum 意为种子，可数义仍是最具体的义项。

senses.title: Cereal crops as a group
senses.definition: cereal crops or their seed considered as a bulk commodity
senses.definitionCN: 作为大宗商品的谷类作物或其种子
senses.example: The port ships grain to three continents.
senses.exampleCN: 这个港口把谷物运往三大洲。
senses.why: An uncountable mass reading grows naturally from many countable seeds handled together.
senses.whyCN: 许多可数种子被一起搬运，自然产生不可数的集合读法。

senses.title: Any small hard particle
senses.definition: a small hard piece of sand, salt, sugar or similar material
senses.definitionCN: 沙、盐、糖或类似物质的一小粒硬块
senses.example: A grain of sand scratched the lens.
senses.exampleCN: 一粒沙子划伤了镜片。
senses.why: The shape of a seed is generalized to any tiny hard body, especially one that can lodge somewhere.
senses.whyCN: 种子的形状被推广到任何微小硬体，尤其是能卡在某处的颗粒。

senses.title: The pattern of fibres
senses.definition: the visible pattern of fibres in wood, stone, leather or cloth
senses.definitionCN: 木材、石材、皮革或织物中可见的纤维纹样
senses.example: The table's grain runs in long parallel lines.
senses.exampleCN: 桌面的纹理呈长长的平行线。
senses.why: Fibres in a material look like rows of seed, so the same word names the visual pattern.
senses.whyCN: 材料中的纤维看起来像一排排种子，于是同一个词也命名视觉纹样。

senses.title: A very small amount
senses.definition: the smallest trace of a quality, as in a grain of truth
senses.definitionCN: 某种品质的最小痕迹，如「一丝真实性」
senses.example: There is a grain of truth in the rumour.
senses.exampleCN: 这则传闻里有一丝真实性。
senses.why: One seed is a tiny unit of a larger mass, and the metaphor turns that into a tiny unit of meaning.
senses.whyCN: 一粒种子是大量物质中的极小单位，比喻把它转为意义的极小单位。

senses.title: A unit of weight
senses.definition: a traditional unit of mass equal to about 64.8 milligrams
senses.definitionCN: 传统质量单位，约等于六十四点八毫克
senses.example: The arrowhead weighed two hundred grains.
senses.exampleCN: 这个箭头重两百格令。
senses.why: Ancient weights were often fixed by counting seeds, and a grain became a standard unit.
senses.whyCN: 古代重量常以数种子的方式确定，一粒便成为标准单位。

senses.title: The rough side of leather
senses.definition: the outer, textured surface of a hide, as opposed to the flesh side
senses.definitionCN: 皮的外层带纹表面，与肉面相对
senses.example: The grain side takes polish better than the flesh side.
senses.exampleCN: 皮面比肉面更容易抛光。
senses.why: The follicles of a hide form a visible grain, so leather workers named the finished side after it.
senses.whyCN: 皮上的毛囊形成可见纹理，因此制皮者以纹理命名朝外的一面。

senses.title: The direction of the fibres
senses.definition: the direction in which wood fibres run, so that one cuts with or against the grain
senses.definitionCN: 木材纤维延伸的方向，因此有顺纹切与逆纹切
senses.example: Planing against the grain tears the surface.
senses.exampleCN: 逆纹刨削会撕裂表面。
senses.why: The pattern and the direction are two views of one thing, and English keeps both as grain.
senses.whyCN: 纹样与走向是同一事物的两种看法，英语把两者都保留为 grain。

intro.en: Grain comes through Old French grain from Latin granum, a seed or kernel. Latin granum continues an Indo-European word for a grain, also seen in corn and kernel. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: grain 经古法语 grain 来自拉丁 granum「种子、谷粒」。拉丁 granum 延续一个表示谷物的印欧词，也出现在 corn 与 kernel 中。年代均为约数。

items.en: Granum meant a seed, a kernel or a small bead; it is the source of grain, granary, granule and granite.
items.cn: granum 意为种子、谷粒或小珠；它是 grain、granary、granule 与 granite 的来源。

items.en: The Indo-European form behind granum is reconstructed from related words and is not directly attested.
items.cn: granum 背后的印欧形式是由相关词重构出来的，并未被直接记录。

items.en: Old French grain carried the word into English after the Norman period, first for cereal seed and then for any small particle.
items.cn: 古法语 grain 在诺曼时期之后把词带入英语，先指谷类种子，后指任何小颗粒。

items.en: By the Middle Ages grain was also a weight fixed by seed count and a word for the surface pattern of wood and leather.
items.cn: 到中世纪，grain 也成了按种子数确定的重量单位，并指木材与皮革的表面纹样。

items.en: Modern trade made the uncountable reading dominant, so grain now often means the whole cereal trade rather than one seed.
items.cn: 现代贸易使不可数读法占主导，于是 grain 现在常指整个谷物贸易，而非一粒种子。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root and first date): the pre-Latin form is reconstructed only, and the earliest English use is dated approximately.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源与首见年代）：拉丁语之前的形式只有重构，英语最早用例的年代也只有约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Latin stock that are easily confused with grain; group two holds words for a seed or a tiny piece.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁词源、易与 grain 混淆的词；第二组是表示种子或微小碎片的词。

entries.definition: A small rounded particle built up from finer material; grain can be a natural seed or any small hard piece.
entries.definitionCN: 由更细材料聚成的小圆粒；grain 可以是天然种子或任何小硬粒。

entries.definition: A building for storing grain, from Latin granarium; it is the place, not the seed.
entries.definitionCN: 储存谷物的建筑，来自拉丁 granarium；它是场所，不是种子。

entries.definition: A coarse-grained rock whose Italian name refers to its granular texture, generally linked to Latin granum.
entries.definitionCN: 一种粗粒岩石，其意大利语名称指颗粒质地，一般认为与拉丁 granum 有关。

entries.definition: A breakfast mixture of oats, nuts and honey; its name is a modern trademark, not a Latin derivative of grain.
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦、坚果与蜂蜜混合的早餐食品；其名称是现代商标，并非 grain 的拉丁派生词。

entries.definition: The unit from which a new plant grows; every grain is a seed, but not every seed is a cereal grain.
entries.definitionCN: 长出新植株的单位；每一粒谷物都是种子，但并非每颗种子都是谷物。

entries.definition: A grass grown for its edible grain; grain is the product, cereal is the plant or the food category.
entries.definitionCN: 为食用谷粒而种植的禾草；grain 是产物，cereal 是植物或食品类别。

entries.definition: The softer edible part inside a husk or shell; a grain may include the husk, while a kernel is what remains inside.
entries.definitionCN: 壳内较软的可食部分；grain 可带壳，而 kernel 指壳内之物。

entries.definition: Any very small piece of matter; grain is usually hard and shaped like a seed.
entries.definitionCN: 任何极小的物质碎片；grain 通常坚硬且形状像种子。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin granum 'seed' is the source of grain, granary, granule and granite.
normal.cn: 拉丁 granum「种子」是 grain、granary、granule 与 granite 的来源。

normal.en: The family runs grain, grainy, graininess, grainless, grained, multigrain.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 grain、grainy、graininess、grainless、grained、multigrain。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: a grain of sand, a grain of truth, wood grain.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：一粒沙、一丝真实、木纹。

normal.en: The phrase against the grain uses the fibre direction sense literally and then figuratively.
normal.cn: 短语 against the grain 先字面使用纤维走向义，再转为比喻。

normal.en: A grain is also a weight, fixed in the past by counting seeds.
normal.cn: grain 还是重量单位，古代以数种子来确定。

abstract.en: Picture one seed held between two fingers while a whole warehouse waits behind it.
abstract.cn: 想象两指间夹着一粒种子，身后是一整座等待的仓库。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden board whose lines run like furrows in a tiny field.
abstract.cn: 想象一块木板，其纹路像微型田里的犁沟。

abstract.en: Picture a rumour weighed on a scale that reads one grain.
abstract.cn: 想象一则传闻放在秤上，读数只有一粒。

examples.en: Store the grain in a dry, sealed bin.
examples.cn: 把谷物存放在干燥密封的仓里。

examples.en: The carpenter sanded along the grain.
examples.cn: 木匠顺着纹理打磨。

examples.en: Take his advice with a grain of salt.
examples.cn: 对他的建议要有所保留。

dict_mnemonic.text: gran（种子、谷粒）→ 一粒谷、一堆谷物、一粒沙、一丝道理；木头的纹路也像一排排种子，所以还指纹理。

root: 拉丁 granum「种子、谷粒」→ 古法语 grain → 英语 grain；granum 的印欧来源属重构形式，同源词包括 corn 与 kernel。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one seed: a seed, a crop, a particle, a fibre pattern, a tiny amount, a weight and two faces of worked leather and wood.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一粒种子展开：种子、作物、颗粒、纤维纹样、极少量、重量单位，以及皮革与木材的两副面孔。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one golden seed lies in a palm, and the same shape reappears as sand, wood grain and a measured unit.
core.cn: 核心意象：一粒金色种子躺在掌心，同一形状又作为沙粒、木纹与计量单位反复出现。

branches.en: THE HARVEST: one seed and the whole crop it belongs to.
branches.cn: 收获：一粒种子与它所属的整片作物。

branches.en: THE PARTICLE: the seed's shape detached from its plant.
branches.cn: 颗粒：种子的形状脱离植物本身。

branches.en: THE SURFACE: fibre pattern and the outer face of leather share one visible texture.
branches.cn: 表面：纤维纹样与皮革外面共享同一种可见质地。

branches.en: THE DIRECTION: the same fibres seen as a line to cut along or across.
branches.cn: 走向：同一纤维被看作可顺切或横切的线。

branches.en: THE MEASURE: a tiny amount of meaning and a tiny unit of mass.
branches.cn: 度量：意义的一丝与质量的一粒。

intro.en: Grain is a Latin noun worn down by French, and its Latin root also builds a technical family in English, so the word can be read from the root outwards.
intro.cn: grain 是经法语磨蚀的拉丁名词，其拉丁词根还在英语中构成一个技术词族，因此可以从词根向外读。

latinIntro.en: Latin granum gives grain directly and supplies granary, granule, granular and granulate; the suffixes -ary, -ule and -ate mark place, small size and making.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 granum 直接给出 grain，并提供 granary、granule、granular 与 granulate；后缀 -ary、-ule 与 -ate 分别标记场所、小尺寸与使成。

items.example: The Latin noun names a single seed.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁名词指单粒种子。

items.structure: grain (English noun, from Old French grain)
items.example: The English word widened far beyond the seed.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语词远远超出种子义。

items.example: The granary held the winter supply.
items.exampleCN: 谷仓存放着冬季口粮。

items.example: A granule of pollen landed on the slide.
items.exampleCN: 一粒花粉落在载玻片上。

items.example: The sugar had a granular texture.
items.exampleCN: 糖呈颗粒质地。

items.example: The machine granulates the fertiliser.
items.exampleCN: 这台机器把肥料造粒。

items.example: The photograph looked grainy in low light.
items.exampleCN: 照片在弱光下显得颗粒粗糙。

items.example: Graininess increased as the film speed rose.
items.exampleCN: 胶片感光度提高，颗粒感也随之增强。

items.example: The multigrain loaf stayed moist for days.
items.exampleCN: 多谷物面包能保持湿润好几天。

definition_zh: 谷类作物；谷物；（英式）谷物早餐
definition_en: a grass grown for its edible grain, the grain itself, or a breakfast food made from such grain
core_image: 早餐桌上的一碗燕麦片，旁边放着麦穗与一袋面粉，三样东西都来自同一种草
scene: 厨房台面上摆着一碗泡了牛奶的燕麦片，旁边是一束干麦穗和一袋面粉。Cereal crops cover more land than any other food group.
sceneCN: 这里指「谷类作物」（第 1 个义项：作为作物类别）；句意为谷类作物占用的土地超过任何其他食物类别。

pos.zh: 谷类作物；谷物；（英式）谷物早餐

derivatives.zh: cereal + grain（组合成分）→ 谷物籽粒（语义偏移：从作物类别缩小到籽粒本身）
cereal + crop（组合成分）→ 谷类作物（语义偏移：强调田间栽培对象）
cereal + bar（组合成分）→ 谷物棒（语义偏移：转为便携食品）
breakfast（早餐）+ cereal → 谷物早餐（语义偏移：专指早餐碗里的加工谷物）
cereal + box（组合成分）→ 谷物包装盒
cereal + bowl（组合成分）→ 谷物碗

senses.title: A grass grown for grain
senses.titleCN: 为收籽粒而种植的禾草
senses.definition: any grass cultivated mainly for its edible starchy grain, such as wheat, rice or maize
senses.definitionCN: 主要为可食淀粉籽粒而栽培的任何禾草，如小麦、稻或玉米
senses.example: Wheat is the cereal best suited to this cold plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 小麦是最适合这块寒冷高原的谷类作物。
senses.why: The word names the plant category, and the botanical link is that all of them are grasses.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名植物类别，其植物学联系在于它们都是禾草。

senses.title: Cereal grain as a mass
senses.definition: the grain of such plants considered as a food or trade commodity
senses.definitionCN: 这类植物的籽粒，作为食品或贸易商品来看
senses.example: Cereal is shipped in bulk from the lake port.
senses.exampleCN: 谷物从这个湖港以散装方式运出。
senses.why: The plant and its product are named by one word because the grain is the reason the plant is grown.
senses.whyCN: 植物与产物用同一个词命名，因为籽粒正是种植它的理由。

senses.title: A breakfast food from grain
senses.definition: a processed breakfast food made from toasted or flaked cereal grains, countable in British usage
senses.definitionCN: 由烘烤或压片的谷物制成的加工早餐食品，英式用法可数
senses.example: The shelf holds six kinds of cereal.
senses.exampleCN: 货架上摆着六种谷物早餐。
senses.why: In the twentieth century the product took the name of its raw material, and British usage made it countable.
senses.whyCN: 二十世纪时产品沿用了原料之名，英式用法又使它可数。

senses.title: A bowl of cereal
senses.definition: a serving of breakfast cereal, usually with milk
senses.definitionCN: 一份谷物早餐，通常加牛奶
senses.example: He eats a bowl of cereal standing up.
senses.exampleCN: 他站着吃一碗谷物早餐。
senses.why: A mass noun can be counted through its container, so a bowl becomes the unit of everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 不可数名词可以借容器计数，于是「一碗」成为日常使用的单位。

senses.title: Grain used as animal feed
senses.definition: cereal grain fed to livestock rather than milled for people
senses.definitionCN: 喂给家畜、而非磨给人吃的谷类籽粒
senses.example: Most of the cereal goes to feed, not to flour.
senses.exampleCN: 大部分谷物用作饲料，而非磨成面粉。
senses.why: The same harvest splits by end use, and feed is the largest destination in many regions.
senses.whyCN: 同一批收成按最终用途分流，在许多地区饲料是最大去向。

senses.title: Adjectival: made from grain
senses.definition: describing a product, field or policy connected with cereal grain
senses.definitionCN: 描述与谷物有关的产品、田地或政策
senses.example: Cereal production rose after the irrigation canal opened.
senses.exampleCN: 灌溉渠开通后谷物产量上升。
senses.why: The noun attributively modifies another noun, a common English way of making a category adjective.
senses.whyCN: 名词作定语修饰另一名词，是英语构成类别形容词的常见方式。

senses.title: A crop in a rotation
senses.definition: a cereal crop considered as one stage in a field rotation
senses.definitionCN: 作为田间轮作一个环节的谷类作物
senses.example: The rotation puts cereal after legumes.
senses.exampleCN: 轮作把谷物安排在豆类之后。
senses.why: Agronomy treats the plant as a slot in a sequence, which gives the word a planning sense.
senses.whyCN: 农学把这种植物当作序列中的一格，于是这个词有了规划义。

senses.title: Grain as a traded commodity
senses.definition: cereal grain priced and traded on markets, often in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 在市场上定价与交易的谷类籽粒，常用复数
senses.example: Cereal prices fell after a record harvest.
senses.exampleCN: 创纪录的收成之后，谷物价格下跌。
senses.why: Trade abstracts the plant into a contract, and the market sense is the most abstract of the eight.
senses.whyCN: 贸易把植物抽象成合约，市场义是八义中最抽象的一层。

intro.en: Cereal comes from Latin cerealis, of Ceres, the Roman goddess of grain, through French céréale. The breakfast sense is a twentieth-century development. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cereal 来自拉丁 cerealis「刻瑞斯的」，刻瑞斯是罗马谷物女神，经法语 céréale 进入英语。早餐义是二十世纪的发展。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ceres was the Roman goddess of grain and harvest, and her name stands at the head of the whole family.
items.cn: 刻瑞斯是罗马的谷物与丰收女神，她的名字位于整个词族的顶端。

items.en: Cerealis meant of Ceres or of grain, and the neuter plural cerealia named her festival and the grain offered at it.
items.cn: cerealis 意为刻瑞斯的或谷物的；中性复数 cerealia 指她的节庆与节上献的谷物。

items.en: French céréale carried the adjective and noun into English in the nineteenth century as a botanical and agricultural term.
items.cn: 法语 céréale 在十九世纪把这个形容词与名词带入英语，作为植物学与农学术语。

items.en: English cereal first named the grain plants, then their grain, and only later the processed breakfast product.
items.cn: 英语 cereal 先指谷类植物，再指其籽粒，最后才指加工后的早餐产品。

items.en: The breakfast food sense grew in the early twentieth century with commercial flaked and puffed cereals, and British usage made it countable.
items.cn: 早餐食品义在二十世纪初随商业化的压片与膨化谷物而发展，英式用法又使其可数。

items.en: Source uncertain (goddess's deeper name): the pre-Latin origin of Ceres is reconstructed and debated, so any Indo-European root offered for it is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（女神名的更深词源）：Ceres 在拉丁语之前的来源属重构且有争议，凡为其给出的印欧词根均属假说。

note.en: Group one holds words that sound like cereal or name its source; group two holds words for grain and grain foods.
note.cn: 第一组是读音像 cereal 或指其来源的词；第二组是表示谷物及谷物食品的词。

entries.definition: A story or set arranged in a series, from Latin series; it sounds identical to cereal but shares no origin.
entries.definitionCN: 按序列编排的故事或一组事物，来自拉丁 series；与 cereal 读音相同，但无共同来源。

entries.definition: The Roman goddess of grain whose name gives cereal; the word is a proper noun, not a food.
entries.definitionCN: 罗马谷物女神，其名给出 cereal；这是专有名词，不是食物。

entries.definition: The seed of a cereal plant; cereal alone can name the plant, the grain or the breakfast food.
entries.definitionCN: 谷类植物的籽粒；单说 cereal 可指植物、谷物或早餐食品。

entries.definition: The seed or the harvested mass; cereal is the plant category or the breakfast product.
entries.definitionCN: 种子或收获后的总量；cereal 是植物类别或早餐产品。

entries.definition: In British English it means the chief local cereal, often wheat; in American English it means maize. Cereal avoids that split.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语指当地主要谷物，常为小麦；美式英语指玉米。cereal 可避开这一分歧。

entries.definition: A sweetened mixture of oats, nuts and dried fruit eaten as a breakfast cereal; it is one product, not the category.
entries.definitionCN: 燕麦、坚果与果干加糖混合的早餐谷物食品；它是单一产品，不是类别。

entries.definition: A hot dish of grain boiled in water or milk; cereal is the raw material or the cold packaged product.
entries.definitionCN: 谷物加水或牛奶煮成的热食；cereal 是原料或冷食包装产品。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Ceres, the grain goddess, stands behind the word.
normal.cn: 谷物女神刻瑞斯站在这个词的背后。

normal.en: The family runs cereal, cereal grain, cereal crop, breakfast cereal, cereal bar.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 cereal、cereal grain、cereal crop、breakfast cereal、cereal bar。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the senses: cereal crops in the field, breakfast cereal in the bowl.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分义项：田里的谷类作物，碗里的谷物早餐。

normal.en: The homophone serial belongs to a different family and means a series.
normal.cn: 同音词 serial 属于另一词族，意为系列。

normal.en: British corn and American corn part company, which is why cereal is the safer category word.
normal.cn: 英式 corn 与美式 corn 分道扬镳，因此 cereal 是更安全的类别词。

abstract.en: Picture a goddess holding one sheaf that becomes a bowl, a bag of flour and a box on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象一位女神手持一束麦穗，它变成一只碗、一袋面粉与货架上的一盒产品。

abstract.en: Picture a field that is also a price chart, each row of stalks a line on the market page.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田同时是一张价格图，每一行麦秆都是行情页上的一条线。

abstract.en: Picture a breakfast table where every object can be traced back to one kind of grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一张早餐桌，每样东西都能追到同一种草。

examples.en: Cereal crops need nitrogen at the start of the season.
examples.cn: 谷类作物在生长季开始时需要氮。

examples.en: She poured the milk over her cereal.
examples.cn: 她把牛奶倒在谷物早餐上。

examples.en: Cereal prices are sensitive to weather in exporting regions.
examples.cn: 谷物价格对出口地区的天气很敏感。

dict_mnemonic.text: Ceres（谷物女神）+ -al（……的）→ 女神的谷物 → 谷类作物、谷物，再到碗里的谷物早餐；与同音的 serial（系列）无关。

root: 拉丁 Ceres（罗马谷物女神，属格 Cereris）+ -alis「……的」→ cerealis「谷物的」→ 法语 céréale → 英语 cereal；Ceres 的更深词源属重构且有争议。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one grass: the plant, its grain, the milled product, the bowl, the feed, the adjective, the rotation slot and the market contract.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种草展开：植物、籽粒、加工产品、碗中之物、饲料、形容词、轮作位置与市场合约。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one kind of grass can become a sheaf, a sack of grain, a bag of flour and a bowl on a breakfast table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一种草可以变成一束麦穗、一袋谷粒、一袋面粉和早餐桌上的一只碗。

branches.en: THE PLANT: the botanical category comes first.
branches.cn: 植物：植物学类别最先出现。

branches.en: THE MASS AND THE MARKET: grain as a bulk food and as a priced contract.
branches.cn: 总量与市场：谷物既是散装食品，也是定价合约。

branches.en: THE BOWL: the processed product and the serving it fills.
branches.cn: 碗：加工产品以及它装满的一份。

branches.en: THE FEED TROUGH: the same harvest diverted to animals.
branches.cn: 饲料槽：同一批收成转向动物。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY LABEL: adjective use and the crop's place in a rotation.
branches.cn: 类别标签：形容词用法与作物在轮作中的位置。

intro.en: Cereal is a Latin adjective turned noun, built from a divine name and a suffix, so its morphology runs through the goddess rather than through a verb.
intro.cn: cereal 是由拉丁形容词转成的名词，由一个神名与后缀构成，因此其构词沿女神名展开，而非沿动词展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin Ceres, genitive Cereris, supplies the stem, and -alis makes the relational adjective cerealis; the neuter plural cerealia named the goddess's festival.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 Ceres（属格 Cereris）提供词干，-alis 构成关系形容词 cerealis；中性复数 cerealia 指女神的节庆。

items.structure: Ceres, Cereris (Latin proper noun, third declension)
items.example: Ceres gave her name to the whole category.
items.exampleCN: 刻瑞斯把名字给了整个类别。

items.example: The suffix builds cerealis from the goddess's name.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由女神名构成 cerealis。

items.example: The adjective described both the goddess and the crop.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词同时描述女神与作物。

items.meaning: a grain plant or its food
items.example: Cereal entered English as a learned term.
items.exampleCN: cereal 作为学术用语进入英语。

items.meaning: the seed of a cereal plant
items.example: The cereal grain is milled into flour.
items.exampleCN: 谷粒被磨成面粉。

items.meaning: a cereal grown in a field
items.example: The cereal crop rotated with beans.
items.exampleCN: 谷类作物与豆类轮作。

items.meaningCN: 加工过的早餐谷物食品
items.example: Breakfast cereal replaced porridge in many homes.
items.exampleCN: 在许多家庭里，谷物早餐取代了粥。

items.example: The cereal bar fits in a coat pocket.
items.exampleCN: 谷物棒能塞进外套口袋。

items.meaning: the packaging of a breakfast cereal
items.example: The cereal box carries the nutrition table.
items.exampleCN: 谷物盒上印着营养表。

definition_en: farm animals kept for use or profit, considered together as a group
core_image: 围栏里牛、羊、马、骆驼挤在一起，耳朵上打着标记，栏外是草场
scene: 围栏门打开，牛群与羊群被赶向草场，耳标在阳光下反光，牧人骑着马在后面压阵。Livestock must be counted before the winter feed is allocated.
sceneCN: 这里指「饲养的家畜整体」（第 1 个义项：牲畜总称）；句意为在分配冬季饲料前必须先清点家畜。

pos.zh: 家畜；牲畜（不可数集合名词）

derivatives.zh: livestock + farming（组合成分）→ 畜牧业（语义偏移：从动物群落到经营行业）
livestock + feed（组合成分）→ 家畜饲料
livestock + producer（组合成分）→ 畜牧生产者
livestock + unit（组合成分）→ 家畜单位（语义偏移：转为统计计量）
livestock + market（组合成分）→ 牲畜市场
livestock + guardian dog（组合成分）→ 护畜犬（语义偏移：指专门守护畜群的犬）

senses.title: Farm animals kept as a group
senses.definition: domesticated animals raised on a farm for food, work, fibre or profit, treated as one category
senses.definitionCN: 为食物、劳作、纤维或利润而在农场饲养的家养动物，作为一个类别看待
senses.example: The farm keeps livestock and grows fodder for them.
senses.exampleCN: 这个农场饲养家畜，并为其种植饲料。
