senses.why: The compound joins live and stock, so the category is literally living property rather than animals seen one by one.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 live 与 stock 结合，因此该类别的字面义是「活着的财产」，而非逐只观看的动物。

senses.title: Cattle in a narrow regional use
senses.definition: cattle specifically, in regions where cattle are the dominant farm animal
senses.definitionCN: 在某些地区特指牛，因为牛是当地主要家畜
senses.example: In that county livestock means cattle, not sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 在那个郡，这个词指牛，而非羊。
senses.why: A general category can be narrowed by local practice until the general word names the commonest member.
senses.whyCN: 泛指类别会被地方实践收窄，直到普通词指最常见的成员。

senses.title: Breeding stock
senses.definition: animals kept to produce young rather than to be sold or worked directly
senses.definitionCN: 为繁殖后代而饲养、而非直接出售或役使的动物
senses.example: Half the herd is breeding livestock kept for replacement heifers.
senses.exampleCN: 这群牛有一半是留作补充母牛的种畜。
senses.why: Stock also means a fund or supply, so animals kept to renew the herd are stock in the strict sense.
senses.whyCN: stock 也有「储备、本钱」之义，因此用于更新畜群的动物正是严格意义上的「本钱」。

senses.title: Animals counted as capital
senses.definition: livestock viewed as a financial asset whose value is recorded and insured
senses.definitionCN: 被视为金融资产、需要记账与投保的家畜
senses.example: The bank valued the livestock before approving the loan.
senses.exampleCN: 银行在批准贷款前对牲畜作了估值。
senses.why: The word's second element already means property, so the financial reading was present from the start.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的第二个成分本就意为财产，因此金融读法从一开始就存在。

senses.title: A herd on pasture
senses.definition: the animals while they are grazing or being moved across land
senses.definitionCN: 正在吃草或正被赶过土地的动物群
senses.example: Livestock graze the high pasture from June to September.
senses.exampleCN: 家畜从六月到九月在高地牧场吃草。
senses.why: The category becomes a moving collectivity when the animals are out on the land.
senses.whyCN: 当动物在土地上移动时，这个类别就变成一个移动的集体。

senses.title: Animals inside a mixed farm
senses.titleCN: 混合农场中的家畜环节
senses.definition: livestock as one component of a system that also grows crops
senses.definitionCN: 作为同时种植作物的系统中的家畜环节
senses.example: Mixed farming uses livestock to cycle nutrients back to the fields.
senses.exampleCN: 混合农业利用家畜把养分循环回田里。
senses.why: In a system, livestock is not only animals but a function: manure, traction and demand for fodder.
senses.whyCN: 在系统中，家畜不只是动物，还是一种功能：粪肥、畜力与对饲料的需求。

senses.title: A source of manure and traction
senses.definition: animals valued for dung, ploughing and transport rather than for meat or milk
senses.definitionCN: 因粪肥、耕地与运输而被重视，而非为肉或奶的动物
senses.example: On the small holding, livestock provide both manure and plough power.
senses.exampleCN: 在这块小地上，家畜同时提供粪肥与犁耕动力。
senses.why: Before engines, the living stock was the farm's energy system, and the word carries that memory.
senses.whyCN: 在发动机之前，活的家畜就是农场的能源系统，这个词带着那段记忆。

senses.title: Animals under herd-health control
senses.titleCN: 畜群健康管理中的家畜
senses.definition: the animals considered as a population to be monitored, vaccinated and quarantined
senses.definitionCN: 被视为需要监测、接种与隔离的动物群体
senses.example: Livestock movement is tracked to control disease.
senses.exampleCN: 为控制疫病，家畜的移动受到追踪。
senses.why: Veterinary medicine treats the herd as one unit, so the collective noun becomes a technical subject.
senses.whyCN: 兽医学把畜群当作一个单位，因此这个集合名词成为技术对象。

intro.en: Livestock is an English compound of live, living, and stock, a supply or fund. It names animals as living property and contrasts with dead stock, the tools and goods on a farm. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: livestock 是英语复合词，由 live「活着的」与 stock「储备、本钱」构成。它把动物命名为「活着的财产」，与 dead stock（农具与货物）相对。年代均为约数。

items.en: Stoc meant a tree trunk, a post or a fixed body, and from that came the sense of a stored supply or a fund.
items.cn: stoc 意为树干、柱子或固定主体，由此引申出「储备、本钱」之义。

items.en: Middle English stock covered goods, money and animals kept as a holding, so the word already implied property.
items.cn: 中古英语 stock 涵盖货物、钱与作为资产饲养的动物，因此这个词已含财产之意。

items.en: The compound live stock separated animals from dead stock, the implements and goods that do not breathe.
items.cn: 复合词 live stock 把动物与 dead stock（不会呼吸的器具与货物）区分开来。

items.en: The compound is recorded in English from the sixteenth century, first in estate accounts and farming manuals.
items.cn: 这个复合词在十六世纪的英语中已有记录，最早见于田产账目与农书。

items.en: Modern agriculture made livestock a sector word covering production, feed, units and health control.
items.cn: 现代农业使 livestock 成为部门词，涵盖生产、饲料、计量单位与健康管理。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact moment when live stock became one written word is not documented, and the deeper origin of stock is reconstructed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：live stock 何时写成一个词没有确切记载，stock 的更早来源也属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on stock or live that are easily confused; group two holds collective words for farm animals.
note.cn: 第一组是由 stock 或 live 构成、易混淆的词；第二组是农场动物的集合名词。

entries.definition: A supply of goods, a fund, or shares in a company; livestock is specifically the living part of a farm's stock.
entries.definitionCN: 货物储备、资金或公司股份；livestock 特指农场储备中活的那部分。

entries.definition: Tools, machinery and unsold goods, the non-living property of a farm; it contrasts directly with livestock.
entries.definitionCN: 工具、机械与未售货物，即农场中非活的部分；与 livestock 直接相对。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning living or not yet dead; alone it does not name animals as property.
entries.definitionCN: 意为活着的、尚未死的形容词；单独使用并不指作为财产的动物。

entries.definition: The means by which someone earns a living; it looks like live plus stock but is built from a different second element.
entries.definitionCN: 某人谋生的手段；看起来像 live 加 stock，但第二个成分不同。

entries.definition: Domesticated bovines as a group; livestock is broader and includes sheep, goats, pigs and horses.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的家牛；livestock 范围更广，还包括羊、山羊、猪与马。

entries.definition: A group of animals of one kind kept together; livestock is a category, a herd is a particular gathering.
entries.definitionCN: 同类动物聚在一起的一群；livestock 是类别，herd 是具体的群。

entries.definition: The everyday phrase for animals kept on a farm; livestock is its formal and commercial equivalent.
entries.definitionCN: 农场饲养动物的日常说法；livestock 是其正式、商业化的对应词。

entries.definition: Animals used to pull ploughs or carts; they are one function of livestock, not the whole category.
entries.definitionCN: 用于拉犁或拉车的动物；它们是家畜的一种功能，而非整个类别。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: live plus stock: living property, as opposed to dead stock.
normal.cn: live 加 stock：活着的财产，与 dead stock 相对。

normal.en: The family runs livestock, livestock farming, livestock feed, livestock unit, livestock market.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 livestock、livestock farming、livestock feed、livestock unit、livestock market。

normal.en: The word is uncountable: one says livestock, not livestocks.
normal.cn: 这个词不可数：说 livestock，不说 livestocks。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the sector: livestock production, livestock sector, livestock guardian dog.
normal.cn: 固定搭配显示部门义：畜牧生产、畜牧部门、护畜犬。

normal.en: The old contrast with dead stock explains why live is inside the word.
normal.cn: 与 dead stock 的旧对照解释了 live 为何在其中。

abstract.en: Picture a farm ledger where animals and tools are written in two separate columns.
abstract.cn: 想象一本农场账簿，动物与工具分列两栏。

abstract.en: Picture a field that eats: the herd is a machine that turns grass into milk and manure.
abstract.cn: 想象一块会吃的田：畜群是一台把草变成奶与粪肥的机器。

abstract.en: Picture a moving warehouse of value, lowing as it crosses the road.
abstract.cn: 想象一座会移动的价值仓库，过马路时发出低鸣。

examples.en: Livestock accounted for half the family's income.
examples.cn: 家畜占了这个家庭收入的一半。

examples.en: The drought forced farmers to sell livestock early.
examples.cn: 干旱迫使农民提前出售家畜。

examples.en: Livestock health checks are required before any animal is moved.
examples.cn: 任何动物移动之前都必须做家畜健康检查。

dict_mnemonic.text: live（活的）+ stock（储备、本钱）→ 活着的本钱，即农场里能繁殖、产奶、干活、卖钱的牲畜总称。

root: live（古英语 libban「活着」）+ stock（古英语 stoc「树干、固定主体」，引申为储备、本钱）；与 dead stock（农具货物）相对，十六世纪起合为一词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one category: animals are first living property, then cattle by region, breeding stock, capital, a grazing herd, a farm function, a source of power and a monitored population.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个类别展开：动物先是活财产，再按地区指牛、种畜、资本、放牧畜群、农场功能、动力来源与被监测的群体。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a farmyard full of breathing property, each animal carrying a mark that says whose it is.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个装满会呼吸的财产的农家院落，每只动物都带着标记，说明它属于谁。

branches.en: THE CATEGORY: all farm animals, or cattle alone where cattle dominate.
branches.cn: 类别：全部农场动物，或在牛占主导的地方单指牛。

branches.en: THE NEXT GENERATION: animals kept to renew the herd.
branches.cn: 下一代：为更新畜群而留的动物。

branches.en: THE LEDGER: animals with a price and an insurance entry.
branches.cn: 账簿：有价格、有保险条目的动物。

branches.en: THE LAND AND THE SYSTEM: grazing herds and the role animals play in mixed farming.
branches.cn: 土地与系统：放牧的畜群，以及动物在混合农业中的角色。

branches.en: POWER AND CONTROL: manure and traction, then vaccination and quarantine.
branches.cn: 动力与控制：粪肥与畜力，然后是接种与隔离。

intro.en: Livestock is a native English compound, not a Latin derivative; its parts are two old Germanic words, and its family is built by compounding.
intro.cn: livestock 是英语本族复合词，并非拉丁派生词；其组成部分是两个古老的日耳曼词，词族靠复合方式扩展。

latinIntro.en: Neither live nor stock has a reliable Latin relative, so the Latin side is left empty; the word's history is Germanic and English.
latinIntro.cn: live 与 stock 都没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁部分留空；这个词的历史属于日耳曼语与英语。

items.example: The first element separates animals from tools.
items.exampleCN: 第一个成分把动物与工具分开。

items.example: The second element supplies the idea of property.
items.exampleCN: 第二个成分提供财产之意。

items.example: Livestock wintered in the lower barn.
items.exampleCN: 家畜在低处的棚里过冬。

items.example: Livestock farming replaced the old wool trade.
items.exampleCN: 畜牧业取代了旧的羊毛贸易。

items.meaning: food grown or mixed for animals
items.meaningCN: 为家畜种植或混合的饲料
items.example: Livestock feed prices rose with the drought.
items.exampleCN: 家畜饲料价格随干旱上涨。

items.meaning: a standard measure of grazing demand
items.meaningCN: 衡量放牧需求的标准单位
items.example: One livestock unit equals one mature cow.
items.exampleCN: 一个家畜单位等于一头成年牛。

items.example: The livestock producer sold directly to the butcher.
items.exampleCN: 这位畜牧生产者直接把畜产品卖给屠户。

items.meaning: a place or trade for buying and selling animals
items.meaningCN: 买卖家畜的场所或交易
items.example: The livestock market opens before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 牲畜市场天亮前开市。

items.meaning: a dog bred to protect a herd
items.example: The livestock guardian dog slept among the sheep.
items.exampleCN: 护畜犬睡在羊群中间。

definition_en: domesticated bovines kept for meat, milk or draught, considered as a herd
core_image: 一群黄牛在草地上低头吃草，几头小牛跟在母牛身边，远处有围栏
scene: 草坡上牛群低头啃草，小牛贴着母牛走，耳标在毛色里格外显眼。Cattle were driven to the high pasture at dawn.
sceneCN: 这里指「作为整体的牛群」（第 1 个义项：牛的总称）；句意为牛群在黎明时被赶往高山牧场。

pos.zh: 牛；牛群（集合名词，复数形式不变）

derivatives.zh: cattle + man（人）→ 养牛人；牧牛者
cattle + drive（驱赶）→ 赶牛（语义偏移：指长距离驱赶牛群）
cattle + grid（格栅）→ 拦牛格栅（语义偏移：指防止牛越过路障的设施）
cattle + ranch（牧场）→ 养牛牧场
cattle + egret（白鹭）→ 牛背鹭（语义偏移：指跟随牛群觅食的鸟）
cattle + cake（饼块）→ 牛用饲料饼

senses.title: Domesticated bovines as a group
senses.definition: cows, bulls and oxen kept by people, considered collectively
senses.definitionCN: 人们饲养的母牛、公牛与阉牛，作为整体看待
senses.example: Cattle grazed the riverside meadow.
senses.exampleCN: 牛群在河边草地上吃草。
senses.why: The word is a collective noun, so it names the group rather than one animal.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是集合名词，因此命名群体而非单只动物。

senses.title: Dairy cattle
senses.definition: cattle kept mainly for milk production
senses.definitionCN: 主要为产奶而饲养的牛
senses.example: Dairy cattle are milked twice a day.
senses.exampleCN: 奶牛每天挤两次奶。
senses.why: Breeds and management split by product, and the plural noun marks the class rather than the species.
senses.whyCN: 品种与管理按产品分流，这个复数名词标记的是类别而非物种。

senses.title: Beef cattle
senses.definition: cattle raised for meat rather than milk or work
senses.definitionCN: 为肉而非奶或劳作饲养的牛
senses.example: Beef cattle finish on grass before the auction.
senses.exampleCN: 肉牛在拍卖前靠草场催肥。
senses.why: The same animal is classified by its economic end, which is why cattle needs a qualifier here.
senses.whyCN: 同一种动物按经济终点分类，因此这里需要用限定词。

senses.title: Draught cattle
senses.definition: cattle trained to pull ploughs, carts or loads
senses.definitionCN: 被训练拉犁、拉车或拉货的牛
senses.example: Draught cattle still work the terraces.
senses.exampleCN: 役用牛仍在梯田上干活。
senses.why: Before tractors, cattle were engines, and the category includes that working role.
senses.whyCN: 在拖拉机之前，牛就是发动机，这个类别包含那种劳作角色。

senses.title: A breeding herd
senses.definition: the cows and bulls kept to produce calves for the herd
senses.definitionCN: 为畜群繁殖小牛而饲养的母牛与公牛
senses.example: The breeding cattle stay on the home pasture.
senses.exampleCN: 繁殖牛群留在自家牧场上。
senses.why: A herd is not only a count but a renewal system, and breeding animals are its core.
senses.whyCN: 畜群不只是数量，还是一套更新系统，繁殖用的牛是它的核心。

senses.title: Cattle as a measure of wealth
senses.definition: cattle owned as property and bridewealth in pastoral and historical societies
senses.definitionCN: 在畜牧与历史社会中作为财产与聘礼的牛
senses.example: The bride price was counted in cattle.
senses.exampleCN: 聘礼以牛计数。
senses.why: Where money is scarce, herds store value, and the collective noun becomes a unit of account.
senses.whyCN: 在货币稀缺之处，畜群储存价值，这个集合名词便成为记账单位。

senses.title: A crowd likened to cattle
senses.titleCN: 被比作牛群的人群（贬义）
senses.definition: a mass of people described as cattle, implying that they move without individual will
senses.definitionCN: 被描述为牛群的人群，暗示他们没有个体意志地移动
senses.example: The refugees were herded like cattle into the sheds.
senses.exampleCN: 难民像牛群一样被赶进棚屋。
senses.why: The metaphor is deliberately degrading: it strips people of individuality by using a herd noun.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻刻意贬低：用畜群名词剥夺人的个体性。

senses.title: A herd counted by head
senses.definition: the agricultural practice of counting cattle individually within a collective noun
senses.definitionCN: 在集合名词内部逐头计数的农业惯例
senses.example: The inspector counted forty head of cattle.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员数了四十头牛。
senses.why: English counts animals by head even when the noun itself refuses a plural, a compromise between group and individual.
senses.whyCN: 英语用「头」来数动物，即使名词本身不加复数，这是群体与个体的折中。

intro.en: Cattle came through Old French catel, property or livestock, from Medieval Latin capitale, a capital holding, from Latin caput, head. It is a doublet of chattel and capital. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: cattle 经古法语 catel「财产、牲畜」来自中世纪拉丁 capitale「资本财产」，再上溯拉丁 caput「头」。它与 chattel、capital 是同源异形词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Caput meant head, and in law and finance it named the principal or the head count of a holding.
items.cn: caput 意为头，在法律与财务中指本金或一笔财产的头数。

items.en: Capitale meant property, stock or principal, especially movable wealth counted by heads of animals.
items.cn: capitale 意为财产、储备或本金，尤指按动物头数计算的动产。

items.en: Old French catel narrowed the learned word to movable property and then especially to livestock.
items.cn: 古法语 catel 把这个学术词收窄为动产，随后尤指牲畜。

items.en: Middle English cattle still meant property in general, and only gradually specialized to bovines.
items.cn: 中古英语 cattle 仍泛指财产，后来才逐渐专门指牛。

items.en: The same Latin source also produced chattel, movable property, and capital, money or principal, so the three words are doublets.
items.cn: 同一拉丁来源还产生 chattel「动产」与 capital「资本、本金」，因此这三个词是同源异形词。

items.en: Source uncertain (first date): the exact period when cattle stopped meaning property and started meaning bovines is not sharply documented.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：cattle 何时不再泛指财产而开始专指牛，缺乏精确记载。

note.en: Group one holds doublets and derived words from the same Latin source; group two holds words for bovines and herds.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁来源的同源异形词与派生词；第二组是表示牛与畜群的词。

entries.definition: A legal word for movable property such as furniture; it comes from the same Old French catel as cattle.
entries.definitionCN: 指家具等动产的法律词；与 cattle 同出古法语 catel。

entries.definition: Money, assets or the head city of a country, from Latin caput; it shares the source of cattle but not its sense.
entries.definitionCN: 资金、资产或首都，来自拉丁 caput；与 cattle 同源但意义不同。

entries.definition: A person who raises or drives cattle; it is the human agent, not the herd.
entries.definitionCN: 饲养或驱赶牛的人；它是人的施动者，不是牛群。

entries.definition: A white egret that follows herds and eats insects they disturb; it is named for its company, not for being cattle.
entries.definitionCN: 跟随牛群、吃被牛惊起的昆虫的白鹭；因与牛为伴而得名，并非牛本身。

entries.definition: The whole category of farm animals; cattle is one member of livestock.
entries.definitionCN: 农场动物的整个类别；cattle 是 livestock 中的一个成员。

entries.definition: A group of animals kept together; cattle names the kind, herd names the gathering.
entries.definitionCN: 聚在一起的一群动物；cattle 命名种类，herd 命名群体。

entries.definition: A single castrated male bovine used for work; cattle is the collective category that contains oxen.
entries.definitionCN: 单头用于劳作的阉公牛；cattle 是包含 oxen 的集合类别。

entries.definition: The scientific adjective for cattle or cattle-like animals; it is a descriptor, not a herd noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指牛或类牛动物的科学形容词；它是描述词，不是畜群名词。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin caput 'head' became property counted by heads, then cattle.
normal.cn: 拉丁 caput「头」变成按头计数的财产，再变成牛。

normal.en: The doublets are cattle, chattel and capital, all from one Latin source.
normal.cn: 同源异形词是 cattle、chattel 与 capital，都来自同一拉丁来源。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the herd: dairy cattle, beef cattle, draught cattle.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分牛群：奶牛、肉牛、役用牛。

normal.en: Cattle is uncountable as a herd but counted by head: forty head of cattle.
normal.cn: cattle 作为畜群不可数，但可按「头」计数：四十头牛。

normal.en: The phrase cattle grid names a barrier, not an animal.
normal.cn: 短语 cattle grid 指一种路障，而非动物。

abstract.en: Picture a herd that is also a bank account, each animal a coin with legs.
abstract.cn: 想象一群牛同时是一个银行账户，每头动物都是一枚有腿的硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd in a station moving with one will, and the word turning cold.
abstract.cn: 想象车站里的人群以一个意志移动，这个词随之变冷。

abstract.en: Picture a field of heads, each one a unit in a ledger.
abstract.cn: 想象一片头的田野，每一个都是账簿上的一单位。

examples.en: The cattle were moved to stubble after the harvest.
examples.cn: 收割后牛群被赶到茬地。

examples.en: Dairy cattle need shade in hot weather.
examples.cn: 奶牛在炎热天气需要遮阴。

examples.en: He owned fifty head of cattle and no land.
examples.cn: 他拥有五十头牛，却没有土地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拉丁 caput（头）→ 按「头」数的财产 → 牛；同源词还有 chattel（动产）与 capital（资本）。

root: 拉丁 caput「头」→ 中世纪拉丁 capitale「财产、本金」→ 古法语 catel「动产、牲畜」→ 英语 cattle；与 chattel、capital 为同源异形词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one herd: a collective animal, then dairy, beef, draught, breeding, wealth, a degrading metaphor and a way of counting heads.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一群牛展开：先是集合动物，再是奶牛、肉牛、役牛、繁殖群、财富、贬义比喻与按头计数的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a herd of bovines stands in a field, and the same herd can be read as milk, meat, power or money.
core.cn: 核心意象：一群牛站在田里，同一群牛可以被读成奶、肉、畜力或金钱。

branches.en: THE COLLECTIVE: one noun for the herd and a head count for its members.
branches.cn: 集合：一个名词指畜群，一个「头」的计数指成员。

branches.en: THE MILK LINE: cattle classified by what they give daily.
branches.cn: 奶线：按每天产出之物分类的牛。

branches.en: MEAT AND POWER: the same animal at the end of its life or in the yoke.
branches.cn: 肉与力：同一动物在生命终点或在轭下。

branches.en: THE NEXT HERD: breeding animals are the system's memory.
branches.cn: 下一群：繁殖动物是这套系统的记忆。

branches.en: VALUE AND INSULT: cattle as bridewealth, and people described as cattle.
branches.cn: 价值与侮辱：作为聘礼的牛，以及被说成牛的人群。

intro.en: Cattle is a French-worn form of a Latin legal noun, and its Latin root also builds two English doublets, so the word can be read through law and property.
intro.cn: cattle 是拉丁法律名词经法语磨蚀的形式，其拉丁词根还构成两个英语同源异形词，因此可以从法律与财产的角度读这个词。

latinIntro.en: Latin caput supplies capitale, which becomes catel in French and cattle in English; the same source yields chattel and capital.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 caput 提供 capitale，在法语中变为 catel，在英语中变为 cattle；同一来源还产生 chattel 与 capital。

items.example: The root names the head that is counted.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根命名被计数的「头」。

items.example: The adjective leads to capital in English.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词在英语中引出 capital。

items.example: Capitale counted wealth by heads of animals.
items.exampleCN: capitale 按动物头数计算财富。

items.example: Old French narrowed the word to property.
items.exampleCN: 古法语把这个词收窄为财产。

items.example: Cattle specialized from property to bovines.
items.exampleCN: cattle 从财产专门化为牛。

items.example: Chattel kept the old property sense.
items.exampleCN: chattel 保留了旧的财产义。

items.example: The cattleman rode the boundary each morning.
items.exampleCN: 养牛人每天早晨巡查边界。

items.meaning: a barrier of bars across a road
items.example: The cattle grid stopped the herd at the gate.
items.exampleCN: 拦牛格栅把牛群挡在门口。

items.meaning: the driving of a herd over distance
items.example: The cattle drive took three days.
items.exampleCN: 赶牛走了三天。

definition_zh: 绵羊；羊（单复数同形）；盲从的人（贬）
definition_en: a woolly domesticated animal kept for wool, meat and milk; a person who follows others without question
core_image: 一群绵羊挤在坡上，毛厚得看不出腿，牧羊犬在边缘绕圈；远处一个人低头跟着人群走
scene: 山坡上的羊群挤成一团，羊毛厚实，牧羊犬贴着边缘来回跑，头羊一动整群就跟着动。Sheep graze the stubble after the grain is cut.
sceneCN: 这里指「绵羊这种动物」（第 1 个义项：家养绵羊）；句意为谷子收割后羊群在茬地里吃草。

pos.zh: 绵羊；羊（单复数同形）；盲从者

derivatives.zh: sheep + -ish（像……的）→ 羞怯的；窘迫的（语义偏移：像羊一样不敢直视人）
sheepish + -ly（副词后缀）→ 羞怯地；窘迫地
sheep + dog（组合成分）→ 牧羊犬
sheep + skin（组合成分）→ 羊皮；羊皮纸
sheep + fold（围栏）→ 羊圈（语义偏移：指围起来的羊栏）
sheep + herd（古英语 hierde「牧人」）→ 牧羊人；引领（语义偏移：由放羊转为照看人群）

senses.title: The woolly domesticated animal
senses.definition: a domesticated ruminant with a thick woolly coat, kept for wool, meat and milk
senses.definitionCN: 一种长着厚羊毛的家养反刍动物，为毛、肉与奶而饲养
senses.example: The sheep wintered under the bank.
senses.exampleCN: 羊群在坡下过冬。
senses.why: The core sense is the animal itself, and English uses one form for one or many.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是动物本身，英语用同一形式表示一只或多只。

senses.title: The species as a kind
senses.definition: the species Ovis aries considered as a kind of animal
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个动物种类的绵羊物种
senses.example: Sheep were domesticated before writing.
senses.exampleCN: 绵羊在文字出现之前已被驯化。
senses.why: A countable animal can also name its whole kind, especially in zoological and historical writing.
senses.whyCN: 可数动物也能命名整个种类，尤见于动物学与历史写作。

senses.title: Animals bred for wool
senses.definition: sheep selected and managed mainly for fleece production
senses.definitionCN: 主要为产毛而选育与管理的羊
senses.example: The merino sheep made the plateau famous.
senses.exampleCN: 美利奴羊使这片高原闻名。
senses.why: Breeds split by product, and wool is the historical reason sheep spread so widely.
senses.whyCN: 品种按产品分流，羊毛是绵羊广泛传播的历史原因。

senses.title: Animals raised for meat
senses.definition: sheep kept to produce mutton and lamb
senses.definitionCN: 为生产羊肉与小羊肉而饲养的羊
senses.example: The upland farms keep sheep for meat.
senses.exampleCN: 高地农场养羊取肉。
senses.why: Meat is the second product, and the word covers the breeding line that supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 肉是第二种产品，这个词涵盖供应它的繁殖线。

senses.title: A flock counted in units
senses.definition: a group of sheep managed and counted together as a flock
senses.definitionCN: 作为一群一同管理与计数的羊
senses.example: The flock numbered three hundred sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 这群羊共有三百只。
senses.why: The animal is normally counted inside a flock, so the singular form serves both one and many.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物通常在羊群内计数，因此单数形式兼指一只与多只。

senses.title: A person who follows blindly
senses.definition: a person who follows the crowd without independent judgment, used as an insult
senses.definitionCN: 不加独立判断而随大流的人，用作侮辱
senses.example: The critics called the voters sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者把选民称为盲从者。
senses.why: The flock's habit of moving as one animal supplies the metaphor: individuals dissolve into the group.
senses.whyCN: 羊群像一只动物那样移动的习惯提供比喻：个体消融在群体中。

senses.title: The flock as a congregation
senses.definition: the biblical image of sheep as a congregation led by a shepherd
senses.definitionCN: 圣经中以羊群比喻由牧者带领的教众
senses.example: The sermon called the parish a flock of sheep.
senses.exampleCN: 布道把教区称为一群羊。
senses.why: Pastoral imagery in scripture made shepherding a model of religious leadership, and the animal carried the metaphor.
senses.whyCN: 经文中的牧羊意象使放牧成为宗教领导的模型，这种动物承载了比喻。

senses.title: The black sheep of a family
senses.definition: a member of a group who is regarded as a disgrace or an oddity
senses.definitionCN: 被群体视为耻辱或异类的成员
senses.example: He was the black sheep of the family.
senses.exampleCN: 他是这个家族里的害群之马。
senses.why: A black fleece is commercially undesirable, so one dark animal in a white flock became an image of deviance.
senses.whyCN: 黑色羊毛在商业上不受欢迎，于是白色羊群中一只黑羊成了离经叛道的形象。

intro.en: Sheep goes back to Old English scēap, from a Germanic word with the same shape. The deeper origin is uncertain; Latin ovis, sheep, is a different root. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: sheep 可上溯到古英语 scēap，来自一个形状相同的日耳曼词。更深的来源不确定；拉丁 ovis「羊」属另一词根。年代均为约数。

items.en: Scēap named the animal and was already used for one or many, a pattern English has kept.
items.cn: scēap 命名这种动物，且已可用于一只或多只，英语保留了这一模式。

items.en: The Germanic form behind scēap is reconstructed from English, Dutch and German evidence rather than recorded directly.
items.cn: scēap 背后的日耳曼形式是由英语、荷兰语与德语证据重构的，而非直接记录。

items.en: The pre-Germanic origin is uncertain; one old suggestion links the word to a root meaning to cut, as the shorn animal, but this is a hypothesis.
items.cn: 日耳曼语之前的来源不确定；一种旧假说把它与表示「剪、切」的词根联系起来，即「被剪毛的动物」，但这只是假说。

items.en: English keeps separate native words for the male ram, the female ewe and the young lamb, while sheep names the kind.
items.cn: 英语为公羊、母羊与羔羊保留各自的本族词，而 sheep 命名整个种类。

items.en: The Bible and pastoral poetry made the flock a model for a congregation, and the insulting sense of a blind follower grew from the same image.
items.cn: 圣经与牧歌把羊群变成教众的模型，而「盲目跟随者」的侮辱义也从同一意象发展出来。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no agreed Indo-European source exists, and any root proposed for the word is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：学界没有公认的印欧来源，凡为此词提出的词根均属重构。

note.en: Group one holds words built on sheep that are easily mistaken for the animal; group two holds the separate words for sheep by age and sex.
note.cn: 第一组是由 sheep 构成、易被误当成动物本身的词；第二组是按年龄与性别区分羊的独立词。

entries.definition: A person who tends sheep, from Old English scēaphierde, sheep herd; it is the keeper, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 照看羊群的人，来自古英语 scēaphierde「羊群牧人」；它是看守者，不是动物。

entries.definition: Looking shy or embarrassed, as if caught doing wrong; it describes a manner, not a sheep.
entries.definitionCN: 显得羞怯或窘迫，像做错事被抓；描述神态，而非羊。

entries.definition: A dog trained to herd sheep; the compound names the helper, not the flock.
entries.definitionCN: 受训驱赶羊群的犬；这个复合词命名助手，而非羊群。

entries.definition: The skin of a sheep with the wool left on, or a parchment made from it; it is a product, not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 保留羊毛的羊皮，或由其制成的羊皮纸；它是产品，不是动物。

entries.definition: An adult female sheep; sheep is the kind, ewe is one sex and age class within it.
entries.definitionCN: 成年母羊；sheep 是种类，ewe 是其中一种性别与年龄等级。

entries.definition: An adult uncastrated male sheep; the word is native and separate from sheep.
entries.definitionCN: 成年未阉割的公羊；这个词是本族词，与 sheep 分开。

entries.definition: A young sheep, or its meat; it names the young stage rather than the species.
entries.definitionCN: 幼羊或其肉；它命名幼年阶段，而非物种。

entries.definition: A horned ruminant kept for milk and meat; it is a different species with different habits and no wool.
entries.definitionCN: 为奶与肉饲养的长角反刍动物；它是不同物种，习性不同且无羊毛。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Sheep is one form for one or many, like deer and fish.
normal.cn: sheep 单复数同形，类似 deer 与 fish。

normal.en: The family runs sheep, sheepish, sheepishly, sheepdog, sheepskin, sheepfold.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 sheep、sheepish、sheepishly、sheepdog、sheepskin、sheepfold。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the uses: a flock of sheep, sheep farming, sheep pasture.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分用法：一群羊、养羊业、羊牧场。

normal.en: The separate words are ram, ewe and lamb, while sheep names the kind.
normal.cn: 分开的词是 ram、ewe 与 lamb，而 sheep 命名种类。

normal.en: Black sheep keeps the wool trade in the metaphor: dark fleece was worth less.
normal.cn: black sheep 把羊毛贸易留在比喻里：深色羊毛价值更低。

abstract.en: Picture a white blanket with legs that turns as one when the dog circles.
abstract.cn: 想象一条有腿的白毯子，狗一绕圈，它就整体转向。

abstract.en: Picture a single dark stitch in a white sleeve and everyone looking at it.
abstract.cn: 想象白色衣袖上的一根深色线，所有人都在看它。

abstract.en: Picture a crowd at a gate, none of them able to say why they are moving.
abstract.cn: 想象门口的人群，没有一个人说得出自己为何在移动。

examples.en: The sheep were dipped before being moved to the lowland.
examples.cn: 羊群在被迁往低地前进行了药浴。

examples.en: Wolves took two sheep from the upper fold.
examples.cn: 狼从上面的羊圈叼走了两只羊。

examples.en: He was the black sheep of a family of doctors.
examples.cn: 在一个医生家族里，他是那个害群之马。

dict_mnemonic.text: sheep 单复数同形；本义是长毛的家养羊，因羊群整体移动，引申出「盲从者」，黑羊则成了「害群之马」。

root: 古英语 scēap「绵羊」，源自原始日耳曼语；更早的印欧来源不确定，凡提出的词根均属重构。拉丁 ovis「羊」属另一词根。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one animal: the woolly grazer, its species, its wool and meat lines, its flock, the blind follower, the congregation and the dark outlier.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种动物展开：长毛的食草者、其物种、产毛与产肉线、羊群、盲从者、教众与深色异类。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a dense white flock moves as one body, and one dark animal stands apart at its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团密集的白羊像一具身体那样移动，一只深色动物独自站在边缘。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL AND THE KIND: one sheep and the species it belongs to.
branches.cn: 动物与种类：一只羊与它所属的物种。

branches.en: FLEECE AND FLESH: the two products that shaped the breeds.
branches.cn: 毛与肉：塑造品种的两种产品。

branches.en: THE FLOCK: the unit in which sheep are actually counted.
branches.cn: 羊群：羊实际被计数的单位。

branches.en: THE FOLLOWER AND THE CONGREGATION: the same flock image used as insult and as scripture.
branches.cn: 跟随者与教众：同一羊群意象既作侮辱，也作经文比喻。

branches.en: THE OUTLIER: one dark fleece marks a member as different.
branches.cn: 异类：一身深色羊毛把某个成员标记为不同。

intro.en: Sheep is a native Germanic noun with no Latin ancestry in English; its family is built from native suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: sheep 是日耳曼本族名词，在英语中没有拉丁祖先；其词族由本族后缀与复合方式构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin relative exists for sheep, since Latin ovis belongs to a different root, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: sheep 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因为拉丁 ovis 属另一词根，所以拉丁部分留空。

items.example: The Old English noun already ignored number.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语名词已不分单复数。

items.example: One sheep stood apart from the flock.
items.exampleCN: 一只羊站在羊群之外。

items.example: The suffix builds sheepish from sheep.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 sheep 构成 sheepish。

items.example: He gave a sheepish grin.
items.exampleCN: 他窘迫地咧嘴一笑。

items.example: The sheepdog held the flock on the path.
items.exampleCN: 牧羊犬把羊群挡在小路上。

items.meaning: a hide with wool, or parchment
items.example: The charter was written on sheepskin.
items.exampleCN: 这份特许状写在羊皮纸上。

items.example: The sheepfold was mended before winter.
items.exampleCN: 羊圈在入冬前修好了。

items.meaning: a keeper of sheep; to guide
items.example: The shepherd counted the flock at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 牧羊人在黄昏清点羊群。

definition_zh: 山羊；山羊皮；（短语中）替罪者；好色的老头（口语旧义）
definition_en: a horned domesticated animal kept for milk, meat and hair; in phrases, a person made to bear blame; an old lecher
core_image: 一只长角的山羊站在陡坡的岩缝上，蹄子扣住石面，身后是几乎垂直的坡
scene: 陡坡上，山羊把蹄子嵌进岩缝，身体几乎贴着石壁向上挪，身后是松动的碎石。Goats can clear brush that cattle cannot reach.
sceneCN: 这里指「山羊这种动物」（第 1 个义项：家养山羊）；句意为山羊能清除牛够不到的灌木。

pos.zh: 山羊；山羊皮；替罪者（短语中）；好色的老头（口语）

derivatives.zh: goat + -ee（指小后缀）→ 山羊胡（语义偏移：指下巴上一小撮像山羊须的胡须）
goat + skin（组合成分）→ 山羊皮；羊皮囊
goat + herd（牧人）→ 牧山羊人
scape（escape 的缩略）+ goat → 替罪羊；使成为替罪者（语义偏移：由仪式中的羊转为承担罪责的人）
goat + cheese（组合成分）→ 山羊奶酪
goat + milk（组合成分）→ 羊奶

senses.title: The horned domesticated animal
senses.definition: a hardy domesticated ruminant with horns and a short coat, kept for milk, meat and hair
senses.definitionCN: 一种耐苦、长角、短毛的家养反刍动物，为奶、肉与毛而饲养
senses.example: The goat climbed the wall as if it were flat ground.
senses.exampleCN: 那只山羊爬墙如同走平地。
senses.why: The core sense is the animal, whose climbing ability is the image behind most of its other uses.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是这种动物，其攀爬能力是它多数其他用法背后的意象。

senses.title: The dairy goat
senses.definition: a goat kept mainly for milk, often in smallholdings and dry regions
senses.definitionCN: 主要为产奶而饲养的山羊，常见于小农与干旱地区
senses.example: The dairy goat gives less milk than a cow but needs far less land.
senses.exampleCN: 奶山羊产的奶比牛少，但所需土地少得多。
senses.why: The animal is classified by its product, and milk is its most efficient contribution on poor land.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物按产物分类，在贫瘠土地上奶是它最有效率的贡献。

senses.title: The meat goat
senses.definition: a goat raised for meat, especially in tropical and subtropical regions
senses.definitionCN: 为肉而饲养的山羊，尤其在热带与亚热带地区
senses.example: The meat goat reaches market weight on browse alone.
senses.exampleCN: 肉用山羊仅靠采食灌木就能达到上市体重。
senses.why: Where cattle cannot thrive, goats convert shrubs into protein, so meat becomes a distinct line.
senses.whyCN: 在牛无法兴旺之处，山羊把灌木转成蛋白质，于是肉成为独立的一条线。

senses.title: The fibre goat
senses.definition: a goat bred for mohair or cashmere hair
senses.definitionCN: 为马海毛或开司米而选育的山羊
senses.example: The fibre goat is combed rather than shorn.
senses.exampleCN: 产毛山羊是梳理取毛，而非剪毛。
senses.why: Hair, not wool, is the product; goats have a double coat and the fine undercoat is the valuable part.
senses.whyCN: 产物是毛而非羊毛；山羊有双层毛被，细软底毛才是珍贵部分。

senses.title: The hide and leather
senses.definition: the skin of a goat, used for leather, parchment and water bags
senses.definitionCN: 山羊的皮，用于皮革、羊皮纸与装水皮囊
senses.example: The water bag was made of goat hide.
senses.exampleCN: 水袋是用山羊皮做的。
senses.why: Goat skin is thin, strong and flexible, which made it a preferred material for books and vessels.
senses.whyCN: 山羊皮薄、韧而柔，因此成为书籍与容器的首选材料。

senses.title: The ritual goat
senses.definition: the goat sent away into the wilderness carrying the sins of the community in the biblical ritual
senses.definitionCN: 圣经仪式中背负群体罪过、被放逐到荒野的羊
senses.example: The ritual goat was driven out on the Day of Atonement.
senses.exampleCN: 在赎罪日，仪式之羊被赶出营地。
senses.why: The Hebrew rite loaded the animal with confessed sins and sent it away, giving English its image of transferred blame.
senses.whyCN: 希伯来仪式把告解的罪放在羊身上并送走，为英语提供了「转移罪责」的意象。

senses.title: A person made to bear blame
senses.definition: a person who is blamed for the faults or mistakes of others
senses.definitionCN: 为他人的过错或失误承担罪责的人
senses.example: The junior clerk became the scapegoat for the lost files.
senses.exampleCN: 初级职员成了文件丢失的替罪羊。
senses.why: The ritual animal's burden transferred to human affairs, where blame is assigned rather than confessed.
senses.whyCN: 仪式动物的负担转到人间事务，在那里罪责是被指派的，而非告解的。

senses.title: An old lecher
senses.definition: an older man regarded as lecherous, an informal and dated use
senses.definitionCN: 被视为好色的年长男子，属口语且过时的用法
senses.example: The old goat was chasing the new secretary.
senses.exampleCN: 那个老色鬼正追逐新来的秘书。
senses.why: The male goat's rutting behaviour supplied a crude metaphor for an older man's pursuit, now mostly dated.
senses.whyCN: 公山羊的发情行为为年长男子的追逐提供了粗俗比喻，如今多已过时。

intro.en: Goat goes back to Old English gāt, from Proto-Germanic gaitaz, from an Indo-European root also seen in Latin haedus, a young goat. Latin capra, a she-goat, is a separate word. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: goat 可上溯到古英语 gāt，来自原始日耳曼语 gaitaz，其印欧词根也见于拉丁 haedus「小山羊」。拉丁 capra「母山羊」则是另一个词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Gāt named the animal in Old English, and the modern goat descends from it with the same meaning.
items.cn: gāt 在古英语中命名这种动物，现代 goat 由它而来，意义未变。

items.en: The Germanic form gaitaz is reconstructed from English, Dutch and German evidence.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 gaitaz 是由英语、荷兰语与德语证据重构的。

items.en: The root behind gaitaz is generally connected with Latin haedus, a young goat, but the exact form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: gaitaz 背后的词根一般认为与拉丁 haedus「小山羊」有关，但确切形式属重构。

items.en: Latin haedus, a kid, shares the old root, while Latin capra, a she-goat, comes from a different word and gives English caprine and Capricorn.
items.cn: 拉丁 haedus「小山羊」共享古老词根，而拉丁 capra「母山羊」来自另一个词，并给出英语 caprine 与 Capricorn。

items.en: The English scapegoat was coined in the sixteenth century from scape, escape, plus goat, translating the ritual animal of Leviticus.
items.cn: 英语 scapegoat 在十六世纪由 scape「escape」加 goat 造出，用来翻译《利未记》中的仪式动物。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Indo-European form is reconstructed, and the exact relation between the Germanic and Latin branches is not settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：印欧形式属重构，日耳曼支与拉丁支的确切关系尚未定论。

note.en: Group one holds compounds and derived words built on goat that are easily mistaken for the animal; group two holds the separate words for goats by age, sex and species.
note.cn: 第一组是由 goat 构成、易被误当成动物本身的复合词与派生词；第二组是按年龄、性别与物种区分山羊的独立词。

entries.definition: A small pointed beard on the chin, named for its resemblance to a goat's tuft; it is not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 下巴上一小撮尖胡须，因形似山羊须而得名；它不是动物。

entries.definition: A person or group made to bear blame for others; the goat is the image, the person is the meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人的过错承担罪责的人或群体；羊是意象，人才是词义。

entries.definition: The skin of a goat, used for leather or a water bag; it is a material, not a living animal.
entries.definitionCN: 山羊的皮，用于皮革或水袋；它是材料，不是活体动物。

entries.definition: A person who tends goats; it is the keeper, not the herd.
entries.definitionCN: 照看山羊的人；它是看守者，不是羊群。

entries.definition: A young goat, or its leather; it names the young stage rather than the species.
entries.definitionCN: 幼山羊或其皮革；它命名幼年阶段，而非物种。

entries.definition: An adult male goat, also used for deer and rabbits; goat names the species, buck names the sex.
entries.definitionCN: 成年公山羊，也用于鹿与兔；goat 命名物种，buck 命名性别。

entries.definition: An adult female sheep; the commonest confusion is to use it for a female goat, which is a doe.
entries.definitionCN: 成年母绵羊；最常见的混淆是拿它指母山羊，而母山羊应为 doe。

entries.definition: A wild mountain goat with long horns; it is a different species from the domesticated goat.
entries.definitionCN: 长角的野生山地山羊；与家养山羊是不同物种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English gāt plus the Germanic root also seen in Latin haedus, a kid.
normal.cn: 古英语 gāt，其日耳曼词根也见于拉丁 haedus「小山羊」。

normal.en: The family runs goat, goatee, goatskin, goatherd, scapegoat, goat cheese.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 goat、goatee、goatskin、goatherd、scapegoat、goat cheese。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the products: goat milk, goat cheese, goat meat.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分产物：羊奶、山羊奶酪、山羊肉。

normal.en: Scapegoat keeps the ritual: blame is loaded on one and sent away.
normal.cn: scapegoat 保留仪式：把罪责装到一只身上并送走。

normal.en: The idiom get someone's goat means to irritate, not to steal an animal.
normal.cn: 习语 get someone's goat 意为惹人生气，不是偷羊。

abstract.en: Picture a hoof finding a crack in a wall where no foot should fit.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蹄子找到墙上本不该容脚的裂缝。

abstract.en: Picture a bundle of blame tied to an animal walking away into the desert.
abstract.cn: 想象一捆罪责绑在一只动物身上，向沙漠走去。

abstract.en: Picture an old man with a pointed beard, and the animal's name doing the insulting.
abstract.cn: 想象一位留着尖胡须的老者，而骂人的是那只动物的名字。

examples.en: The goat cleared the blackberry thicket in a week.
examples.cn: 山羊一周就清完了黑莓灌木丛。

examples.en: Goat cheese has a sharper taste than cow cheese.
examples.cn: 山羊奶酪比牛奶酪味道更尖。

examples.en: The manager was made the scapegoat for a decision he had opposed.
examples.cn: 经理成了他本就反对的那项决定的替罪羊。

dict_mnemonic.text: goat（山羊）+ -ee（指小）→ goatee 山羊胡；scape（escape）+ goat → 被放走的替罪羊；山羊能爬陡坡，也引申出「老色鬼」。

root: 古英语 gāt「山羊」→ 原始日耳曼 gaitaz；其印欧词根一般认为与拉丁 haedus「小山羊」有关，属重构形式；拉丁 capra「母山羊」为另一词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one climber: the animal, its milk, meat and hair, its hide, the ritual burden, the blamed person and a dated insult.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个攀爬者展开：动物本身、奶、肉与毛、皮、仪式负担、被指责的人，以及一个过时的骂法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a horned animal stands on a crack in a cliff, and the same animal can be milk, meat, hair, leather or a burden of blame.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只长角动物站在崖壁裂缝上，同一只动物可以是奶、肉、毛、皮革或一捆罪责。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: the hardy climber is the source of every other sense.
branches.cn: 动物：耐苦的攀爬者是其他所有义项的源头。

branches.en: MILK AND MEAT: two ways the animal feeds people on poor land.
branches.cn: 奶与肉：这种动物在贫瘠土地上养人的两种方式。

branches.en: HAIR AND HIDE: the coat and the skin become cloth and leather.
branches.cn: 毛与皮：毛被与皮肤变成织物与皮革。

branches.en: THE BURDEN: the ritual animal becomes the human scapegoat.
branches.cn: 负担：仪式动物变成人间替罪者。

branches.en: THE INSULT: the male animal's behaviour supplies a crude metaphor.
branches.cn: 骂法：公羊的行为提供了一个粗俗比喻。

intro.en: Goat is a native Germanic noun; its compounds are made with ordinary English elements, and its Latin relatives belong to a different branch of the same old root.
intro.cn: goat 是日耳曼本族名词；其复合词由普通英语成分构成，拉丁同族词属于同一古老词根的另一分支。

latinIntro.en: Latin haedus, a kid, shares the old root, while capra, a she-goat, is a separate word; both are given below because both are useful for reading the family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 haedus「小山羊」共享古老词根，而 capra「母山羊」是另一个词；两者都列在下面，因为两者都有助于读出这个词族。

items.example: The Old English noun is the direct ancestor.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语名词是直接祖先。

items.structure: goat (English noun, from Old English gāt)
items.example: The goat browsed the young trees.
items.exampleCN: 山羊啃食了小树。

items.example: His goatee made his face look longer.
items.exampleCN: 他的山羊胡让脸显得更长。

items.example: The goatskin flask kept the water cool.
items.exampleCN: 羊皮水壶让水保持凉爽。

items.example: The goatherd led the herd down the scree.
items.exampleCN: 牧羊人把羊群带下碎石坡。

items.meaning: one who bears blame for others
items.example: The report made the driver the scapegoat.
items.exampleCN: 报告把司机变成了替罪羊。

items.example: Goat cheese ripens faster than cow cheese.
items.exampleCN: 山羊奶酪比牛奶酪熟得快。

items.example: Goat milk is easier to digest for some people.
items.exampleCN: 对某些人来说羊奶更容易消化。

items.meaning: a wild goat of rocky mountains
items.example: The mountain goat crossed the ledge without slowing.
items.exampleCN: 山地野山羊毫不减速地走过岩檐。

definition_zh: 马；骑兵；体操鞍马；锯木架；晾衣架；马力（口语）
definition_en: a large domesticated animal used for riding and draught; cavalry; a frame or device named after the animal; a unit of engine power
core_image: 一匹马在草地上奔跑，鬃毛扬起；旁边是一个木制锯木架，四条腿撑开
scene: 草场上马蹄翻起泥点，鬃毛被风扯向后方，骑手压低身体；场边摆着四条腿撑开的木架。The horse carried the rider across the flooded ford without hesitation.
sceneCN: 这里指「用于骑乘的马」（第 1 个义项：马这种动物）；句意为这匹马毫不犹豫地把骑手驮过漫水的浅滩。

pos.zh: 马；骑兵；体操鞍马；锯木架；晾衣架
胡闹（仅用于短语 horse around）

collocations.zh: 黑马；出人意料的竞争者

derivatives.zh: horse + man（人）→ 骑马者；马术师
horseman + -ship（技艺、身份）→ 马术（语义偏移：从人转为技艺）
horse + back（背）→ 马背；骑马地
horse + drawn（被拉的）→ 马拉的
horse + hair（毛）→ 马毛；马鬃毛（语义偏移：指制刷与制弓的材料）
horse + power（动力）→ 马力（语义偏移：由动物力转为工程计量单位）
horse + play（玩耍）→ 嬉闹；粗野的胡闹（语义偏移：像马一样撒欢）

senses.title: The riding and draught animal
senses.definition: a large domesticated mammal with hooves and a mane, used for riding, racing and pulling loads
senses.definitionCN: 一种有蹄与鬃毛的大型家养哺乳动物，用于骑乘、赛马与拉载
senses.example: The horse stood still while the saddle was tightened.
senses.exampleCN: 紧鞍带时那匹马站着一动不动。
senses.why: The animal is the core sense, and its speed and strength are the source of every derived use.
senses.whyCN: 动物本身是核心义，它的速度与力量是所有引申用法的源头。

senses.title: Horses as a kind
senses.definition: the species Equus caballus considered collectively
senses.definitionCN: 作为一个物种整体看待的马
senses.example: Horses were reintroduced to the steppe after a long absence.
senses.exampleCN: 马在长期缺席之后被重新引入草原。
senses.why: A countable animal also names its whole kind, especially in history and biology.
senses.whyCN: 可数动物也能命名整个种类，尤见于历史与生物学。

senses.title: Cavalry soldiers
senses.definition: soldiers who fight on horseback, treated as a branch of an army
senses.definitionCN: 骑马作战的士兵，作为军队的一个兵种看待
senses.example: The horse broke the infantry line at dusk.
senses.exampleCN: 骑兵在黄昏突破了步兵阵线。
senses.why: Metonymy replaces the rider with the mount, so a whole military branch is called horse.
senses.whyCN: 转喻用坐骑替代骑手，于是整个兵种被称为 horse。

senses.title: A gymnastic vaulting horse
senses.definition: a padded apparatus that gymnasts vault over or swing on
senses.definitionCN: 体操运动员翻越或支撑摆动的软包器械
senses.example: She scored highest on the horse.
senses.exampleCN: 她在鞍马上得分最高。
senses.why: The apparatus inherited the animal's shape, a padded body on four legs, and kept its name.
senses.whyCN: 这种器械继承了动物的形状——四条腿撑着一个软包躯体，并保留了它的名字。

senses.title: A sawhorse
senses.definition: a wooden trestle with four legs used to support timber while it is cut
senses.definitionCN: 四条腿的木支架，锯木材时用来承托
senses.example: The plank rested on two sawhorses.
senses.exampleCN: 木板搁在两个锯木架上。
senses.why: Any four-legged support looks like a standing horse, so the animal's name moved to workshop furniture.
senses.whyCN: 任何四条腿的支架都像一匹站立的马，于是动物之名移到作坊家具上。

senses.title: A clothes horse
senses.definition: a frame for hanging or drying clothes indoors
senses.definitionCN: 室内挂晾衣物的框架
senses.example: The laundry filled the clothes horse by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 中午时晾衣架已经挂满了衣物。
senses.why: The frame is another four-legged stand, and the same image spread from the yard to the laundry.
senses.whyCN: 这又是一个四条腿的架子，同一意象从院子扩展到洗衣房。

senses.title: A unit of engine power
senses.definition: a conventional unit of power originally based on the work a draught horse could do
senses.definitionCN: 一种传统功率单位，最初以役马能做的功为基准
senses.example: The old engine produced forty horsepower.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧发动机输出四十马力。
senses.why: Engineers needed a familiar yardstick, so one horse's output became a unit for machines.
senses.whyCN: 工程师需要一个熟悉的尺子，于是以一匹马的输出作为机器的单位。

senses.title: To fool around
senses.definition: to behave noisily or irresponsibly, used in the phrase horse around
senses.definitionCN: 喧闹或不负责地胡来，用于短语 horse around
senses.example: The boys horsed around until the teacher arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩们一直胡闹到老师来。
senses.why: A loose horse galloping without purpose supplies the image of uncontrolled play.
senses.whyCN: 一匹脱缰的马无目的地奔跑，提供了「失控玩耍」的意象。

intro.en: Horse goes back to Old English hors, from Proto-Germanic hrossa, from a root generally connected with the idea of running. Latin currere, to run, belongs to the same old root. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: horse 可上溯到古英语 hors，来自原始日耳曼语 hrossa，其词根一般认为与「奔跑」有关。拉丁 currere「跑」属于同一古老词根。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hors named the animal in Old English and also stood for cavalry, a use English keeps in the phrase horse and foot.
items.cn: hors 在古英语中命名这种动物，也指骑兵，英语在短语 horse and foot 中保留了这一用法。

items.en: The Germanic form hrossa is reconstructed from English, German and Dutch evidence rather than recorded directly.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 hrossa 是由英语、德语与荷兰语证据重构的，而非直接记录。

items.en: The word is generally connected with a root meaning to run, the same source as Latin currere and cursus.
items.cn: 这个词一般认为与表示「跑」的词根有关，与拉丁 currere 和 cursus 同源。

items.en: Latin currere, to run, and cursus, a course, come from the same old root, which is why they are useful relatives for the English word.
items.cn: 拉丁 currere「跑」与 cursus「行程」来自同一古老词根，因此它们是这个英语词的有用同族。

items.en: From the sixteenth century four-legged stands took the name, and from the eighteenth the animal's work rate became horsepower.
items.cn: 十六世纪起四条腿的支架取得这个名字；十八世纪起，动物的做功速率变成马力。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Indo-European form is reconstructed, and the exact relation between hrossa and currere is not demonstrated in detail.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：印欧形式属重构，hrossa 与 currere 的确切关系也没有得到详细证明。

note.en: Group one holds horse compounds that are easily mistaken for the animal; group two holds the separate words for horses by sex, size and use.
note.cn: 第一组是由 horse 构成、易被误当成动物本身的复合词；第二组是按性别、体型与用途区分马的独立词。

entries.definition: A person who rides or manages horses; it is the human agent, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 骑马或管理马的人；它是人的施动者，不是动物。

entries.definition: The back of a horse, or the act of riding; it names a place or posture, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 马背，或骑马的状态；它命名位置或姿势，不是动物。

entries.definition: A unit of power based on a horse's work rate; it is a measurement, not a horse.
entries.definitionCN: 以马的工作速率为基础的功率单位；它是计量，不是马。

entries.definition: Rough noisy fun; it uses the horse as an image of uncontrolled movement, not as a subject.
entries.definitionCN: 粗野喧闹的玩闹；它把马当作失控运动的意象，而非主体。

entries.definition: An adult female horse; horse names the kind, mare names the sex.
entries.definitionCN: 成年母马；horse 命名种类，mare 命名性别。

entries.definition: An adult uncastrated male horse; it is a sex class within the species.
entries.definitionCN: 成年未阉割的公马；它是物种内的性别等级。

entries.definition: A small horse breed, usually under a fixed height; it is a size class, not a separate species.
entries.definitionCN: 体型较小的马品种，通常低于规定高度；它是体型等级，不是独立物种。

entries.definition: An animal, often a horse, that one rides; it is the role in riding, not the species.
entries.definitionCN: 供人骑乘的动物，常为马；它是骑乘中的角色，不是物种。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English hors is connected with running, the same root as Latin currere.
normal.cn: 古英语 hors 与奔跑有关，与拉丁 currere 同根。

normal.en: The family runs horse, horseman, horseback, horsepower, horsehair, horseplay.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 horse、horseman、horseback、horsepower、horsehair、horseplay。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the uses: ride a horse, horse racing, horse-drawn.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分用法：骑马、赛马、马拉的。

normal.en: Four-legged stands keep the animal's shape: sawhorse and clothes horse.
normal.cn: 四条腿的支架保留了动物的形状：锯木架与晾衣架。

normal.en: Cavalry is simply horse in military writing, as in horse and foot.
normal.cn: 在军事文本中骑兵就是 horse，如 horse and foot。

abstract.en: Picture a body of muscle that can be read as speed, rank, furniture or engine power.
abstract.cn: 想象一具肌肉之躯，可以被读成速度、军阶、家具或发动机功率。

abstract.en: Picture a wooden trestle standing in a yard, waiting to be ridden by a plank.
abstract.cn: 想象一个木架站在院子里，等着被一块木板「骑」。

abstract.en: Picture a child galloping through a kitchen until the table shakes.
abstract.cn: 想象一个孩子跑过厨房，直到桌子都晃起来。

examples.en: The horse refused the jump at the last stride.
examples.cn: 那匹马在最后一步拒绝起跳。

examples.en: Cavalry horses were kept in the rear until the signal.
examples.cn: 骑兵的马留在后方，直到信号出现。

examples.en: He would not stop horsing around during the rehearsal.
examples.cn: 排演时他不停地胡闹。

dict_mnemonic.text: horse 本义是马，因马有四条腿，四腿木架也叫 horse；因马能出力，功率单位叫 horsepower；骑兵也用 horse 代称。

root: 古英语 hors「马」→ 原始日耳曼 hrossa；一般认为与表示「奔跑」的词根有关，拉丁 currere「跑」与 cursus「行程」同源，更早形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one animal: the mount, the species, the cavalry, two kinds of frame, a unit of power and a way of playing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种动物展开：坐骑、物种、骑兵、两种架子、功率单位与一种玩闹方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a running animal and a four-legged wooden stand share one outline, and the same outline appears in a gymnasium and a laundry.
core.cn: 核心意象：奔跑的动物与四条腿的木架共享一个轮廓，同一轮廓又出现在体操房与洗衣房。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL AND THE KIND: one horse and the species it belongs to.
branches.cn: 动物与种类：一匹马与它所属的物种。

branches.en: THE WAR MOUNT: the rider is replaced by the horse in military speech.
branches.cn: 战马：军事语言中用马替代骑手。

branches.en: THE GYMNASTIC FRAME: a padded body on four legs keeps the shape.
branches.cn: 体操器械：四条腿上的软包躯体保留了形状。

branches.en: THE WORK FRAME: sawhorse and clothes horse are the animal turned furniture.
branches.cn: 工作架：锯木架与晾衣架是动物变成家具。

branches.en: POWER AND PLAY: the horse's work rate becomes a unit, and its loose gallop becomes a game.
branches.cn: 力与玩：马的工作速率变成单位，脱缰奔跑变成游戏。

intro.en: Horse is a native Germanic noun, and its large compound family is built from English elements rather than Latin suffixes.
intro.cn: horse 是日耳曼本族名词，其庞大的复合词族由英语成分而非拉丁后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word is its direct ancestor, but Latin currere and cursus share the old running root; Latin equus names the animal from a different root and is given for contrast.
latinIntro.cn: 没有拉丁词是它的直接祖先，但拉丁 currere 与 cursus 共享古老的「跑」词根；拉丁 equus 从另一词根命名这种动物，列在此处作对照。

items.example: The Old English noun already had both senses.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语名词已有两种意义。

items.structure: horse (English noun, from Old English hors)
items.example: The horse cleared the ditch easily.
items.exampleCN: 那匹马轻松越过沟。

items.example: The horseman rode ahead of the column.
items.exampleCN: 骑马者骑在队伍前面。

items.example: Her horsemanship impressed the judges.
items.exampleCN: 她的马术让评委印象深刻。

items.meaning: the back of a horse; riding
items.example: They travelled on horseback.
items.exampleCN: 他们骑马旅行。

items.example: A horse-drawn cart blocked the lane.
items.exampleCN: 一辆马车挡住了小路。

items.meaning: hair from a horse's mane or tail
items.example: The bow was strung with horsehair.
items.exampleCN: 那把弓用马毛上弦。

items.example: The pump needs ten horsepower.
items.exampleCN: 这台泵需要十马力。

items.example: Horseplay broke the window.
items.exampleCN: 胡闹打碎了窗户。

definition_zh: 骆驼；驼色；驼毛织物；船用浮筒
definition_en: a large long-necked desert mammal with humps; a fawn colour; a fabric made from camel hair; a float used in salvage
core_image: 一只双峰骆驼站在沙丘脊线上，影子被夕阳拉长，驼峰投下两团阴影
scene: 沙丘脊线上，骆驼缓慢抬脚，宽大的蹄掌陷进沙里又拔出，驼队在后面连成一线。A camel can cross the dunes without water for days.
sceneCN: 这里指「沙漠中的骆驼」（第 1 个义项：骆驼这种动物）；句意为骆驼可以连续数日不饮水穿越沙丘。

pos.zh: 骆驼；驼色；驼毛织物；船用浮筒

collocations.zh: 骆驼的鼻子（比喻得寸进尺的开端）

derivatives.zh: camel + -id（科名后缀）→ 骆驼科动物；骆驼科的（语义偏移：由单一物种升为科级分类）
camel + hair（毛）→ 驼毛；驼毛织物
camel + back（背）→ 驼峰形坡；驼背（语义偏移：指形似驼峰的地形或结构）
camel + corps（部队）→ 骆驼兵部队
camel + train（队列）→ 骆驼队
camel + thorn（刺）→ 骆驼刺（语义偏移：指骆驼常吃的带刺植物）

senses.title: The desert mammal
senses.definition: a large long-necked mammal with one or two humps, adapted to hot dry country
senses.definitionCN: 一种长颈、有一或两个驼峰的大型哺乳动物，适应炎热干旱地区
senses.example: The camel stored fat in its hump, not water.
senses.exampleCN: 骆驼把脂肪储在驼峰里，而不是水。
senses.why: The animal is the core sense, and its hump is the image behind most other uses.
senses.whyCN: 动物本身是核心义，驼峰是多数其他用法背后的意象。

senses.title: The two main kinds
senses.definition: the one-humped dromedary and the two-humped Bactrian, the two domesticated kinds
senses.definitionCN: 单峰驼与双峰驼这两种主要家养种类
senses.example: The Bactrian camel tolerates colder winters than the dromedary.
senses.exampleCN: 双峰驼比单峰驼更能忍受寒冷的冬天。
senses.why: A single word covers both kinds because they do the same work in the same landscapes.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词涵盖两种，因为它们在相同景观中做同样的工作。

senses.title: The pack animal of caravans
senses.definition: a camel used to carry goods and people across desert routes
senses.definitionCN: 在沙漠路线上驮运货物与人的骆驼
senses.example: The caravan lost two camels in the sandstorm.
senses.exampleCN: 商队在沙暴中丢了两峰骆驼。
senses.why: The animal's economic role became a sense of its own: not the species but the transport unit.
senses.whyCN: 这种动物的经济角色独立成义：不是物种，而是运输单位。

senses.title: Camel-hair cloth
senses.definition: a soft cloth made from camel hair, often used for coats
senses.definitionCN: 用驼毛制成的柔软织物，常用于大衣
senses.example: The coat was lined with camel hair.
senses.exampleCN: 这件大衣用驼毛作衬。
senses.why: The animal's coat became a textile named after its source, then a colour named after the textile.
senses.whyCN: 动物的毛被变成以来源命名的织物，随后又变成以织物命名的颜色。

senses.title: The colour camel
senses.definition: a light yellowish-brown colour like untreated camel hair
senses.definitionCN: 像未染色驼毛那样的浅黄褐色
senses.example: The walls were painted a warm camel.
senses.exampleCN: 墙壁被刷成温暖的驼色。
senses.why: Textiles often give their colour names to the wider world, and camel hair supplied a whole palette.
senses.whyCN: 织物常把颜色名给更广的世界，驼毛提供了一整套色系。

senses.title: A camel corps
senses.definition: a military unit mounted on camels for desert patrol
senses.definitionCN: 骑骆驼在沙漠巡逻的军事单位
senses.example: The camel corps patrolled the frontier wells.
senses.exampleCN: 骆驼兵部队巡查边境的水井。
senses.why: Like horse for cavalry, camel can stand for the soldiers mounted on it.
senses.whyCN: 如同 horse 可指骑兵，camel 也可指骑骆驼的士兵。

senses.title: A marine salvage float
senses.definition: a watertight float placed under a sunken vessel to lift it
senses.definitionCN: 放在沉船下方以将其抬起的密封浮筒
senses.example: Divers attached four camels to the wreck.
senses.exampleCN: 潜水员把四个浮筒固定在沉船上。
senses.why: The float carries a load the way a camel does, so naval engineers borrowed the animal's name.
senses.whyCN: 浮筒像骆驼一样承载重物，因此海军工程师借用了动物之名。

senses.title: The camel's nose under the tent
senses.titleCN: 骆驼的鼻子（得寸进尺的开端）
senses.definition: a small initial intrusion that is allowed to grow into a full takeover
senses.definitionCN: 最初被容许的小侵入，最终长成全面占据
senses.example: The first exception was the camel's nose.
senses.exampleCN: 第一个例外就是那只伸进帐篷的骆驼鼻子。
senses.why: The fable of a camel asking to put its nose inside a tent, then taking the whole tent, became a political image.
senses.whyCN: 骆驼请求把鼻子伸进帐篷、最后占据整个帐篷的寓言，成了政治意象。

intro.en: Camel comes through Latin camelus and Greek kamelos from a Semitic word also seen in Hebrew gamal and Arabic jamal. English borrowed it early from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: camel 经拉丁 camelus 与希腊 kamelos 来自一个闪米特词，也见于希伯来语 gamal 与阿拉伯语 jamal。英语很早就从拉丁语借入。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hebrew gamal and Arabic jamal name the camel, and the shape of the word points to a shared Semitic origin.
items.cn: 希伯来语 gamal 与阿拉伯语 jamal 都指骆驼，其词形指向共同的闪米特来源。

items.en: Greek borrowed the Semitic word as kamelos, and the Greek form is the route through which the animal reached Europe.
items.cn: 希腊语借入这个闪米特词为 kamelos，这条希腊形式是把这种动物带到欧洲的路径。

items.en: Latin camelus came from Greek and named both the animal and, in some texts, a camel-hair rope or covering.
items.cn: 拉丁 camelus 来自希腊语，既指这种动物，也在某些文本中指驼毛绳或覆盖物。

items.en: Old English camel came from Latin, and the word has kept its animal sense unchanged for centuries.
items.cn: 古英语 camel 来自拉丁语，这个词的动物义数百年未变。

items.en: The textile and colour senses grew in modern English, while the naval float was named by engineers who saw a load-bearing shape.
items.cn: 织物与颜色义在现代英语中发展，海军浮筒则由工程师看到承重形状而得名。

items.en: Source uncertain (Semitic route): the exact Semitic form behind Greek kamelos is not settled, and more than one reconstruction is proposed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（闪米特路径）：希腊 kamelos 背后的确切闪米特形式尚未定论，学界提出不止一种重构。

note.en: Group one holds camel compounds and derived words that are easily mistaken for the animal; group two holds the camel family and its working role.
note.cn: 第一组是由 camel 构成、易被误当成动物本身的复合词与派生词；第二组是骆驼科成员及其劳作角色。

entries.definition: Any member of the camel family, including llamas and alpacas; camel is one genus within it.
entries.definitionCN: 骆驼科的任何成员，包括美洲驼与羊驼；camel 是其中一属。

entries.definition: The hair of a camel or cloth made from it; it is a textile, not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 骆驼的毛或由其制成的布；它是织物，不是动物。

entries.definition: A ridge or bridge shaped like a hump; it borrows the animal's outline, not its body.
entries.definitionCN: 形似驼峰的山脊或桥；它借的是动物轮廓，不是身体。

entries.definition: A spiny shrub that camels browse; it is named for its eaters, not for being a camel.
entries.definitionCN: 骆驼采食的带刺灌木；因食客而得名，并非骆驼本身。

entries.definition: The one-humped domesticated camel of hot regions; camel is the broader word covering both kinds.
entries.definitionCN: 炎热地区单峰的家养骆驼；camel 是涵盖两者的更广的词。

entries.definition: The two-humped camel of colder Central Asian regions; it is a kind of camel, not a separate word for the species.
entries.definitionCN: 中亚较冷地区的双峰骆驼；它是骆驼的一种，不是物种的另一个词。

entries.definition: A South American camelid used as a pack animal; it shares the family but not the desert adaptation.
entries.definitionCN: 南美骆驼科动物，用作驮畜；它同科，但没有沙漠适应特征。

entries.definition: Any animal used to carry loads; camel is the most famous desert example of the role.
entries.definitionCN: 任何用于驮运的动物；骆驼是这一角色最著名的沙漠例子。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek kamelos and Latin camelus came from a Semitic word for the animal.
normal.cn: 希腊 kamelos 与拉丁 camelus 来自一个指这种动物的闪米特词。

normal.en: The family runs camel, camelid, camelhair, camelback, camel train, camel corps.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 camel、camelid、camelhair、camelback、camel train、camel corps。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the uses: camel hair, camel coat, camel train.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分用法：驼毛、驼色大衣、骆驼队。

normal.en: The hump is the key image: camelback names anything shaped like it.
normal.cn: 驼峰是关键意象：camelback 命名任何形似驼峰之物。

normal.en: The camel's nose fable explains the political sense of a small intrusion.
normal.cn: 骆驼鼻子寓言解释了「小侵入」的政治义。

abstract.en: Picture a ship of the desert that carries a whole household on its back.
abstract.cn: 想象一艘沙漠之舟，把整个家当都驮在背上。

abstract.en: Picture a coat the colour of the animal that supplied the cloth.
abstract.cn: 想象一件大衣，颜色正是提供布料的动物之色。

abstract.en: Picture a nose entering a tent, and the tent later belonging to the nose.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鼻子伸进帐篷，后来帐篷归了那只鼻子。

examples.en: The camel drank enough to last a week.
examples.cn: 那峰骆驼喝足了能撑一周的水。

examples.en: She wore a camel coat over a dark dress.
examples.cn: 她在深色连衣裙外穿了一件驼色大衣。

examples.en: The salvage team lifted the barge with four camels.
examples.cn: 打捞队用四个浮筒把驳船抬了起来。

dict_mnemonic.text: camel（骆驼）→ 驼毛 camelhair → 驼色 camel；因能驮重物，打捞浮筒也叫 camel；骆驼鼻子伸进帐篷的寓言成了「得寸进尺」。

root: 闪米特语词（希伯来 gamal、阿拉伯 jamal）→ 希腊 kamelos → 拉丁 camelus → 古英语 camel；希腊形式背后的确切闪米特词形属重构且有多种假说。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one desert animal: the mammal, its two kinds, its caravan work, its hair, its colour, its military use, a salvage float and a fable.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一种沙漠动物展开：哺乳动物、两个种类、商队劳作、驼毛、驼色、军事用途、打捞浮筒与一则寓言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a humped animal walks a dune ridge, and the hump reappears as cloth, colour, a float and a small intruding nose.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只带峰的动物走在沙丘脊线上，驼峰又作为织物、颜色、浮筒与一只探入的鼻子反复出现。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL AND ITS KINDS: one word covers both the one-humped and two-humped forms.
branches.cn: 动物与种类：同一个词涵盖单峰与双峰两种。

branches.en: THE CARAVAN AND THE CORPS: the animal as transport, civilian and military.
branches.cn: 商队与部队：作为运输工具的动物，民用与军用。

branches.en: HAIR AND COLOUR: the coat becomes cloth, and the cloth becomes a palette.
branches.cn: 毛与色：毛被变成织物，织物又变成色系。

branches.en: THE FLOAT: a load-bearing shape borrows the animal's role.
branches.cn: 浮筒：承重形状借用了动物的角色。

branches.en: THE WEDGE: a fable about a nose explains a small takeover.
branches.cn: 楔子：一则关于鼻子的寓言解释小规模占据。

intro.en: Camel is a borrowed word with a short Latin layer and a productive English compound family; it has no native Germanic root in English.
intro.cn: camel 是借词，有一层简短的拉丁成分与一个能产的英语复合词族；它在英语中没有本族日耳曼词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin camelus came from Greek kamelos, and the suffix -inus appears in the Latin adjective for camel-like things; modern English builds the rest with -id and compounds.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 camelus 来自希腊 kamelos，后缀 -inus 出现在表示「像骆驼的」拉丁形容词中；现代英语用 -id 与复合方式构成其余部分。

items.example: Greek carried the Semitic word into Europe.
items.exampleCN: 希腊语把这个闪米特词带入欧洲。

items.example: Latin camelus is the direct source of English camel.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁 camelus 是英语 camel 的直接来源。

items.example: The camel knelt to be loaded.
items.exampleCN: 骆驼跪下让人装货。

items.example: The suffix builds camelid from camel.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由 camel 构成 camelid。

items.meaning: a member of the camel family
items.example: The llama is a camelid.
items.exampleCN: 美洲驼是骆驼科动物。

items.example: The brush was set in camelhair.
items.exampleCN: 这把刷子用驼毛制成。

items.example: The road climbed a camelback.
items.exampleCN: 道路爬上一道驼峰形山脊。

items.example: The camel train crossed at night.
items.exampleCN: 骆驼队在夜间穿过。

items.example: The camel corps held the oasis.
items.exampleCN: 骆驼兵部队守住了绿洲。

definition_en: a castrated adult male bovine used for draught; a bovine animal in compounds
core_image: 两头阉公牛并排套在木轭上，肩背隆起，拉着犁在硬土里前进
scene: 两头阉公牛并排套进木轭，肩峰顶住横木，犁铧在硬土里翻出连续的土块。The ox team pulled the plough to the field's far edge.
sceneCN: 这里指「套轭耕田的阉公牛」（第 1 个义项：役用阉公牛）；句意为这对耕牛把犁拉到田的最远端。

derivatives.zh: ox + -en（古英语复数词尾）→ 阉公牛的复数（语义偏移：保留强变化复数）
ox + herd（牧人）→ 牧牛人
ox + cart（车）→ 牛车
ox + bow（弯木）→ 牛轭弯木；河曲（语义偏移：指形似牛轭的河湾）
ox + hide（皮）→ 牛皮
ox + eye（眼）→ 牛眼菊（语义偏移：指花盘像牛眼的花）
ox + blood（血）→ 深红色（语义偏移：指像牛血的颜色）

senses.title: A castrated adult male bovine
senses.definition: an adult male bovine that has been castrated, usually for work
senses.definitionCN: 已阉割的成年公牛，通常用于劳作
senses.example: The ox was quieter than the bull beside it.
senses.exampleCN: 这头阉牛比旁边的公牛安静。
senses.why: The core sense is a sex-and-work class, not simply a male bovine.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个性别与劳作等级，而非单纯的雄性牛。

senses.title: A draught animal in a team
senses.definition: an ox trained to pull a plough, cart or load, usually paired with another
senses.definitionCN: 受训拉犁、拉车或拉货的牛，通常与另一头配对
senses.example: The team of oxen turned the heavy soil in long lines.
senses.exampleCN: 这对耕牛拉着长线翻动重土。
senses.why: Castration made the animal tractable, so work is the reason the class exists.
senses.whyCN: 阉割使动物温顺，因此劳作是这个等级存在的理由。

senses.title: A bovine in compounds
senses.definition: a general bovine reference in compounds such as oxhide, ox tongue or ox-eye
senses.definitionCN: 在 oxhide、ox tongue、ox-eye 等复合词中泛指牛
senses.example: The drum was stretched with oxhide.
senses.exampleCN: 这面鼓用牛皮蒙成。
senses.why: In compounds the sex distinction fades, and ox becomes a plain word for the animal's body or products.
senses.whyCN: 在复合词中性别区分淡化，ox 变成指动物身体或产物的普通词。

senses.title: Ox meat and parts
senses.definition: the meat or edible parts of an ox, as in ox tongue or ox cheek
senses.definitionCN: 阉牛的肉或可食部位，如牛舌、牛颊
senses.example: The ox tongue was boiled with herbs.
senses.exampleCN: 牛舌与香草一起煮。
senses.why: The working animal also enters the kitchen, and its name survives on cuts and dishes.
senses.whyCN: 役用动物也进入厨房，其名留在肉块与菜肴上。

senses.title: The zodiac Ox
senses.definition: the second sign of the Chinese zodiac, rendered in English as the Ox
senses.definitionCN: 中国生肖的第二位，英语译作 the Ox
senses.example: The Year of the Ox began with the new moon.
senses.exampleCN: 牛年随新月开始。
senses.why: Translation chose the farm ox as the English name for a zodiac branch, and the image stuck.
senses.whyCN: 翻译选用农家的牛作为某个生肖地支的英语名，这个意象固定下来。

senses.title: A very strong person
senses.definition: a person compared to an ox for strength or patient endurance
senses.definitionCN: 因力量或耐性而被比作牛的人
senses.example: He was strong as an ox and just as silent.
senses.exampleCN: 他力大如牛，也一样沉默。
senses.why: The ox's strength and patience, not its intellect, supply the comparison.
senses.whyCN: 提供比较的是牛的力气与耐性，而非智力。

senses.title: A yoke as a pair
senses.definition: a pair of oxen joined by one yoke, treated as a working unit
senses.definitionCN: 由同一副轭连成一对、作为一个劳作单位的牛
senses.example: A yoke of oxen could plough an acre in a day.
senses.exampleCN: 一对同轭耕牛一天能犁一英亩。
senses.why: The harness, not the animal, becomes the unit, and English counts ploughing by the yoke.
senses.whyCN: 成为单位的是轭具而非动物，英语按「轭」计算犁地。

senses.title: A sacrificial animal
senses.definition: an ox offered in classical or biblical sacrifice
senses.definitionCN: 在古典或圣经祭祀中献上的牛
senses.example: The temple accepted a perfect ox without blemish.
senses.exampleCN: 神庙接受一头无瑕的牛。
senses.why: The ox was the costliest common sacrificial animal, which is why the word appears in ritual law.
senses.whyCN: 牛是最昂贵的常见祭牲，因此这个词出现在祭祀律法中。

intro.en: Ox goes back to Old English oxa, from Proto-Germanic uhsō(n), from an Indo-European word for ox or bull. The plural oxen preserves an old strong ending. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: ox 可上溯到古英语 oxa，来自原始日耳曼语 uhsō(n)，再上溯一个表示牛或公牛的印欧词。复数 oxen 保留古老强变化词尾。年代均为约数。

items.en: Oxa named the castrated male bovine, and the plural oxan already showed the old ending.
items.cn: oxa 指阉割的雄性牛，复数 oxan 已显示古老词尾。

items.en: The Germanic form is reconstructed from English, German and Old Norse evidence.
items.cn: 这个日耳曼形式是由英语、德语与古诺斯语证据重构的。

items.en: The root behind ox is a separate bovine word from the root that gives Latin bos and Greek bous, so the two families are not close relatives.
items.cn: ox 背后的词根与给出拉丁 bos、希腊 bous 的词根属于不同的「牛」词，因此两个词族并非近亲。

items.en: The plural oxen keeps a strong noun ending that most English nouns have lost, which is why the form looks irregular.
items.cn: 复数 oxen 保留多数英语名词已丢失的强变化词尾，因此这个形式看起来不规则。

items.en: The animal's role as a plough team and as a sacrifice gave English the phrases a yoke of oxen and the sacrificial ox.
items.cn: 这种动物作为犁队与祭牲的角色，给英语留下「一轭牛」与「祭牛」的说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the Indo-European form is reconstructed, and its relation to the other bovine roots is not settled.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词根）：印欧形式属重构，它与其他「牛」词根的关系尚未定论。

note.en: Group one holds ox compounds that are easily mistaken for the animal; group two holds the separate words for bovine age, sex and use.
note.cn: 第一组是由 ox 构成、易被误当成动物本身的复合词；第二组是按年龄、性别与用途区分牛的独立词。

entries.definition: The U-shaped collar of an ox yoke, or a river bend of that shape; it is not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 牛轭的 U 形弯木，或形似它的河湾；它不是动物。

entries.definition: A daisy-like flower with a large yellow centre, named for its ox-eye look; it is a plant.
entries.definitionCN: 花盘大而黄、形似牛眼的花；它是植物。

entries.definition: A cart pulled by oxen; it names the vehicle, not the team.
entries.definitionCN: 由牛拉的车；它命名车辆，不是牛队。

entries.definition: A person who tends oxen; it is the keeper, not the animal.
entries.definitionCN: 照看牛的人；它是看守者，不是动物。

entries.definition: An adult uncastrated male bovine; an ox is a bull that has been castrated for work.
entries.definitionCN: 成年未阉割的公牛；ox 是已为劳作而阉割的公牛。

entries.definition: A young castrated male bovine, often raised for beef; ox is usually older and trained to work.
entries.definitionCN: 年轻的阉公牛，常为肉用；ox 通常更年长且受训劳作。

entries.definition: A young bull or a castrated bull, especially in British regional use; it overlaps with ox but is usually younger.
entries.definitionCN: 年轻公牛或阉公牛，尤见于英国方言；与 ox 重叠，但通常更年轻。

entries.definition: Bovines as a group; ox names one castrated working animal within the herd.
entries.definitionCN: 作为整体的牛；ox 指牛群中一头阉割的役用牛。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English oxa and the old plural oxan explain the irregular oxen.
normal.cn: 古英语 oxa 与旧复数 oxan 解释了不规则的 oxen。

normal.en: The family runs ox, oxen, oxherd, oxcart, oxbow, oxhide, oxeye.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 ox、oxen、oxherd、oxcart、oxbow、oxhide、oxeye。

normal.en: Fixed phrases split the uses: a yoke of oxen, ox cart, ox hide.
normal.cn: 固定搭配区分用法：一对同轭牛、牛车、牛皮。

normal.en: Ox is a castrated bull, not any bull; the knife made it workable.
normal.cn: ox 是阉过的公牛，不是任何公牛；是刀使它可用。

normal.en: The zodiac Ox is a translation choice, not a biological category.
normal.cn: 生肖牛是翻译选择，不是生物学类别。

abstract.en: Picture two heavy bodies joined by one wooden bar, moving as a single machine.
abstract.cn: 想象两具沉重的身体被一根木杠连成一台机器。

abstract.en: Picture a river bending back on itself like a yoke left in the grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一条河弯回自身，像遗在草里的牛轭。

abstract.en: Picture a silent man carrying what four others cannot lift.
abstract.cn: 想象一个沉默的人扛起四个人抬不动的东西。

examples.en: A yoke of oxen pulled the stone boat.
examples.cn: 一对同轭耕牛拉着石船。

examples.en: The oxen were fed before the people.
examples.cn: 先喂牛，再喂人。

examples.en: He was strong as an ox but slow to anger.
examples.cn: 他力大如牛，却不易发怒。

dict_mnemonic.text: ox 是阉过的成年公牛，复数 oxen；套上轭就是耕牛，因此有 a yoke of oxen；牛皮、牛舌、牛眼菊都用它作限定成分。

root: 古英语 oxa「阉公牛」→ 原始日耳曼 uhsō(n) → 印欧牛词；复数 oxen 保留古强变化词尾。该词根与拉丁 bos、希腊 bous 不同源，更早形式属重构。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one working animal: the castrated male, the draught team, the generic bovine, meat, the zodiac, strength, the yoke as a unit and the sacrifice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一头役用动物展开：阉公牛、役畜队、泛指牛、牛肉、生肖、力气、以轭为单位与祭牲。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy animal stands under a wooden yoke, and the yoke turns it into a unit of power.
core.cn: 核心意象：一头沉重的动物站在木轭下，木轭把它变成一单位动力。

branches.en: THE ANIMAL: castration defines the class before any work begins.
branches.cn: 动物：在开始任何劳作之前，阉割先定义了等级。

branches.en: THE TEAM: the pair under one yoke is the ploughing unit.
branches.cn: 牛队：同轭的一对是犁地单位。

branches.en: THE BODY: in compounds and in the kitchen, ox becomes plain bovine flesh.
branches.cn: 身体：在复合词与厨房里，ox 变成普通的牛肉与牛身。

branches.en: THE ZODIAC: translation turns the farm animal into a calendar sign.
branches.cn: 生肖：翻译把农场动物变成历法符号。

branches.en: STRENGTH AND SACRIFICE: the same body is admired for power and offered in ritual.
branches.cn: 力气与祭祀：同一具身体既因力量被赞叹，也在仪式中被献上。

intro.en: Ox is a native Germanic noun with an old irregular plural; its family is built by compounding, not by Latin suffixes.
intro.cn: ox 是日耳曼本族名词，带一个古老的不规则复数；其词族靠复合而非拉丁后缀构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin relative exists for ox, since Latin bos and Greek bous belong to a different bovine root, so the Latin side is left empty.
latinIntro.cn: ox 没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因为拉丁 bos 与希腊 bous 属于另一「牛」词根，所以拉丁部分留空。

items.example: The Old English noun already meant the working animal.
items.exampleCN: 这个古英语名词已指役用动物。

items.example: The ending survives only in a few nouns such as oxen.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾只保留在少数名词中，如 oxen。

items.structure: ox (English noun, from Old English oxa)
items.example: The ox pulled the cart without complaint.
items.exampleCN: 这头牛毫无怨言地拉车。

items.example: The oxen were yoked before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 牛在天亮前被套上轭。

items.example: The oxherd slept beside the stall.
items.exampleCN: 牧牛人睡在牛栏旁。

items.example: The oxcart carried the harvest home.
items.exampleCN: 牛车把收成运回家。

items.meaning: a yoke's U-shaped collar; a river bend
items.example: The river left an oxbow in the meadow.
items.exampleCN: 河在草地上留下一个牛轭弯。

items.example: The shield was covered with oxhide.
items.exampleCN: 盾面蒙着牛皮。

items.example: Oxeye daisies filled the verge.
items.exampleCN: 牛眼菊长满了路旁。

definition_zh: 犁；耕地；艰难推进；扫雪机；投入（资金）
definition_en: a farm tool that turns over soil; to turn soil; to move with force through something; a snowplow; to reinvest money
core_image: 犁铧切开草皮，翻出的土块整齐倒向一侧，后面跟着拉犁的牲口
scene: 铁犁切进草皮，土块顺着犁壁翻倒，草根朝上，后面跟着两头拉犁的牲口。The plow turns the stubble under before the winter rains.
sceneCN: 这里指「翻土的犁具」（第 1 个义项：农具犁）；句意为犁在冬雨前把茬子翻到土下。

pos.zh: 耕地；艰难推进；猛撞；投入（资金）

derivatives.zh: plow + -ing（动作名词）→ 耕地作业
plow + -ed（过去分词）→ 已耕的
plow + man（人）→ 犁地的人
plow + share（犁刀）→ 犁铧（语义偏移：指犁的切土部件）
plow + land（土地）→ 可耕地；犁地量（语义偏移：历史上作土地面积单位）
snow（雪）+ plow → 扫雪机；扫雪（语义偏移：把犁的动作用于清雪）

senses.title: The farm implement
senses.definition: a farm tool with a blade that cuts and turns over the soil before sowing
senses.definitionCN: 播种前切开并翻动土壤的带刃农具
senses.example: The plow was dragged to the field's edge.
senses.exampleCN: 犁被拖到田边。
senses.why: The implement is the core sense, and its shape, a blade plus a beam, drives every later extension.
senses.whyCN: 农具本身是核心义，其形状——刃加横梁——推动所有后来的扩展。

senses.title: To turn over the soil
senses.definition: to cut and turn the soil with a plough before planting
senses.definitionCN: 种植前用犁切开并翻动土壤
senses.example: They plow the lower field in November.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在十一月翻耕低处的田。
senses.why: The tool becomes a verb by the ordinary English route: use the object, and the object's name becomes the action.
senses.whyCN: 工具按英语常见路径变成动词：使用该物，其名便成为动作。

senses.title: To move with effort through something
senses.definition: to advance slowly and forcefully through snow, traffic, a crowd or a long text
senses.definitionCN: 在雪、交通、人群或长文中缓慢而用力地前进
senses.example: She plowed through the report before the meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她在会前费力读完了报告。
senses.why: A plough pushes resistance aside in a straight line, and that feeling transfers to any difficult passage.
senses.whyCN: 犁把阻力推向一边并直线前进，这种感觉转移到任何艰难的通过。

senses.title: A snowplow, or to clear snow
senses.definition: a vehicle or blade for pushing snow off a road, or the act of clearing snow with one
senses.definitionCN: 把雪推离道路的车辆或铲板，或用其清雪的行为
senses.example: The snowplow opened the pass by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 扫雪机在中午前打通了山口。
senses.why: The machine does exactly what a plough does to soil, so the name moved from field to road.
senses.whyCN: 机器对雪做的事正是犁对土做的事，于是名字从田里移到路上。

senses.title: To crash into something
senses.definition: to collide violently with something, used in the phrase plow into
senses.definitionCN: 猛烈撞上某物，用于短语 plow into
senses.example: The truck plowed into the barrier.
senses.exampleCN: 卡车猛撞上护栏。
senses.why: The image is force meeting resistance without slowing, the same image as a blade entering soil.
senses.whyCN: 意象是力量遇到阻力却不减速，与刀刃进入土壤同一意象。

senses.title: To reinvest money
senses.definition: to put profits or savings back into a business or project
senses.definitionCN: 把利润或储蓄重新投入企业或项目
senses.example: They plowed the first year's profit into new equipment.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把第一年的利润投入新设备。
senses.why: Money is turned into the ground of a business the way a field is turned before a new crop.
senses.whyCN: 资金被翻进企业的基础，如同新一季作物之前翻田。

senses.title: The Plough asterism
senses.definition: the group of seven stars also called the Big Dipper, seen as a plough shape
senses.definitionCN: 又称北斗七星的七颗星，被看作犁的形状
senses.example: The Plough stood almost overhead at midnight.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜时北斗七星几乎在头顶。
senses.why: The seven stars trace a blade and a beam, so English and Irish sky lore named them after the tool.
senses.whyCN: 七颗星勾出刃与梁的形状，因此英语与爱尔兰的星空传说以农具命名它们。

senses.title: A historical land measure
senses.titleCN: 历史上的耕地面积单位
senses.definition: ploughland, a unit of land that one plough team could work in a year
senses.definitionCN: 犁地量：一队犁牛一年能耕完的土地单位
senses.example: The manor was assessed at five ploughlands.
senses.exampleCN: 这座庄园被估为五个犁地量。
senses.why: Land was measured by the work needed to till it, so the tool's name became an area unit.
senses.whyCN: 土地按耕作所需的工作量计量，因此工具之名成为面积单位。

intro.en: Plow goes back to Old English plōg, probably reinforced by Old Norse plógr, from Proto-Germanic plōgaz. The deeper origin is uncertain; a link to a Celtic word for a heavy plough is one hypothesis. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: plow 可上溯到古英语 plōg，可能受古诺斯语 plógr 强化，来自原始日耳曼语 plōgaz。更早来源不确定；与凯尔特语表示重犁之词的关联是假说之一。年代均为约数。

items.en: Plōg named the soil-turning implement, and the word already carried the sense of the work as well as the tool.
items.cn: plōg 命名翻土农具，这个词已同时带有工具与劳作两种意思。

items.en: Old Norse plógr, used by Scandinavian settlers, probably reinforced the English form and its spelling.
items.cn: 斯堪的纳维亚移民使用的古诺斯语 plógr 可能强化了英语形式及其拼写。

items.en: The Germanic form plōgaz is reconstructed from English and Norse evidence rather than recorded directly.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 plōgaz 是由英语与诺斯语证据重构的，而非直接记录。

items.en: The pre-Germanic origin is uncertain; a link to a Celtic term for a heavy plough has been suggested, and Latin plaustrum, a wagon, is sometimes mentioned, but neither is established.
items.cn: 日耳曼语之前的来源不确定；有人提出与凯尔特语表示重犁的词有关，也有人提到拉丁 plaustrum「车」，但两者都未获证实。

items.en: British English settled on plough while American English kept plow, so the same word has two standard spellings today.
items.cn: 英式英语定为 plough，美式英语保留 plow，因此今天同一个词有两种标准拼写。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): no agreed pre-Germanic source exists, so any root offered for the word is a reconstruction or a hypothesis.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：没有公认的日耳曼语之前来源，凡为此词提出的词根均属重构或假说。

note.en: Group one holds forms and compounds built on plow that are easily mistaken for the tool; group two holds verbs and nouns for working the soil.
note.cn: 第一组是由 plow 构成、易被误当成农具本身的词形与复合词；第二组是表示翻土作业的动词与名词。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same word; it is not a different tool but a spelling variant.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写；它不是另一种农具，而是拼写变体。

entries.definition: The cutting blade of a plough; it is one part of the tool, not the whole.
entries.definitionCN: 犁的切土刀片；它是工具的一部分，不是整体。

entries.definition: A person who ploughs; it is the worker, not the implement.
entries.definitionCN: 犁地的人；它是劳动者，不是农具。
